title: Graph Compounding
body:
I'm focusing on the "breakeven line" idea and its ability to accurately express when a position is compounded (yield is withdrawn, and redeposited.) Instead of graphing it as a ray (a line with one "extended" point) we can instead graph it as a line segment (no extended points) from the position deposit time, to when a position's size is modified. 

If we add to the position size, then the breakeven line should be steeper (more fees should be accrued due to a larger position size.) I made a quick mockup using TradingView to illustrate this idea.

title: Dynamic Data Input
body:
# Dynamic Data Input on TradingView Indicator

The first major engineering challenge in order for this to be useful in realtime decision making is to allow for the script to have the capability to dynamically read position data from external data sources. I did quite a bit of research on this, and it appears that TradingView's PineScript does not currently have this capability. 

Currently the variables must be manually input on the indicator. This can be done by double clicking the indicator on TradingView.

![tv](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4975670/201572439-f6443b3e-5f1c-4abc-bc15-e8a0be86a129.jpg)

Those variables are manually imported off of the data presented by Revert's UI

https://revert.finance/#/uniswap-position/mainnet/312741

The founder of Revert passed me along this draft documentation of their private API. This was current as of 12 July 2022, as such there may have been some changes introduced since. This will allow you to access the information in JSON format. 

[apidocs.md](https://github.com/ubiquity/uniswap-v3-liquidity-provider-indicator/files/9999366/apidocs.md)

---

# Research

I would encourage you to explore workarounds.

### Workaround Strategy A - API Reverse Engineering

I would highly recommend API reverse engineering so that there is FAR LESS infrastructure to support for this capability. Then we could have a super simple node program that simply pings Revert (GET) and TradingView (POST) APIs every minute or so.

### Workaround Strategy B - Scraper

Have a remote invoked [scraper](http://github.com/ubiquity/scraper) to manually log in to your TradingView account, and

1. pass in the updated parameters using the settings panel (this might be possible by directly making the API request to update the user's settings vs having to navigate through the UI) or 
2. to hardcode the parameters and update the PineScript code.

title: Adding collateral enabled checks for redemption collections might make users uncapable of redeming their funds.
body:
[MEDIUM] - Adding collateral enabled checks for redemption collections might make users uncapable of redeming their funds.

This PR is intended to fix [the bug described in this Sherlock issue](https://github.com/sherlock-audit/2023-12-ubiquity-judging/issues/29). However, the Sherlock report is actually wrong and the vulnerability described must not be considered as an issue in the first place, so the collateralEnabled check should not be added on collecting redemptions.

Enabling/disabling collaterals allows the protocol to add or remove supported collaterals, not to be used under uncertain situations, such as a hack. In such type of situations, the `isRedeemPaused` check can be enabled to prevent users from redeeming if something wrong is currently  happening.

The problem with adding the `collateralEnabled` check here is that if Ubiquity decides to disable a collateral in the future, some redemptions might be already queued, so users won't be able to withdraw their funds.


Recommendation: Remove the `collateralEnabled` check for collecting redemptions.

_Originally posted by @0xadrii in https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/pull/894#discussion_r1572571068_

Lucia Browser SDK – Integration Spec (Wix / WordPress / Shopify / Framer)

🎯 Objective

Enable non-technical users (e.g. IG influencers, small merchants) to install Lucia SDK via a simple script embed, enabling automatic tracking of page views, button clicks, and scrolls.

🧩 Core Requirements

1. Universal Embed Script

  • Provide a single <script> tag to paste into Wix / WordPress / Shopify / Framer settings.

  • Example:

    

<script src="https://cdn.luciaprotocol.com/lucia-sdk-latest.min.js"></script>
<script>
  LuciaSDK.init({
    // API Key from https://ads.clickinsights.xyz
    api_key: 'bbbbbbbb-a7298818-3265d018-e9a648ae-95371b44-d25e6c77-38069b79-1e4bd263'
  });

  LuciaSDK.pageView('PAGE-NAME');
</script>

  • SDK auto-initializes via LuciaSDK.init()

2. Auto Page Tracking

  • SDK automatically triggers:

    LuciaSDK.pageView('projects')

  • Should debounce duplicate triggers (e.g., single-page app reloads or Wix internal router updates).

3. Button Click Tracking

  • Auto-attach click listeners to all visible <button> and <a> elements.

  • On click:

    LuciaSDK.buttonClick({
  ...
});

4. Scroll Tracking

  • Emit event when user scrolls past key thresholds (5%,10%,15%, 20%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%):

    LuciaSDK.trackScroll({ event: 'scroll', value: scrollDepth });

5. Attribution Context

Every event includes:

{
  "utm": getUtmParams(),
  "device": getBrowserData().device,
  "screen": getBrowserData().screen,
  "browser": getBrowserData().browser
}

6. CMS-Specific Implementation Notes

Platform | Implementation Path | Notes -- | -- | -- Wix | Paste JS into Site Settings → Tracking & Analytics (Runs on all pages). | Fallback: per-page embed if global not available. WordPress | Add script via Header/Footer plugin or functions.php. | Compatible with both Classic & Gutenberg editors. Shopify | Add to theme.liquid before . | Use window.ShopifyAnalytics.meta to enrich attribution data. Framer | Paste via Custom Code → Footer Script. | SPA-friendly — detect route changes via window.onpopstate.

User Story 📸

As an IG influencer with a Wix site,
I want to install Lucia SDK by pasting one script,
So I can see which buttons and pages my visitors interact with
— without needing to code or configure tracking manually.

User Story ⛴️

As an e-commerce store owner with a Shopify site, among other sites like Amazon
I want to install Lucia SDK by pasting one script,
So I can track conversion rate on major buttons for purchasing, track conversion rates on other minor buttons like contact form fill outs, and pages my visitors interact with
— without needing to code extensively or configure tracking page by page.

✅ Deliverables

  • CDN-ready build sdk.min.js

  • Cross-platform event tracking (page, click, scroll)

  • Docs examples for Wix, WordPress, Shopify, Framer

  • Event schema alignment with backend fingerprints table

title: Passively Collect All Emails
body:
# Detect “email-ish” fields with a scored heuristic + runtime signals. 

input[type=email]

input[type=text|search], textarea whose name/id/class include: email, e-mail, mail, login, user, username, handle, contact, work_email, business_email

autocomplete hints: email, username

Associated <label for=...> or ARIA text containing: email, e-mail, work email, business email, school email, username, handle

pattern attributes that include @ or typical email regex fragments

placeholder text with @ or “email”, “username”

### Steps Summarized

1. Detect likely email fields (reuse your detector).
2. Attach listeners (change, blur, submit, paste).
3. Validate & normalize the value (RFC-5322-ish regex + trim/lowercase).
4. Respect consent/config (don’t capture if disallowed).
5. Queue and send to API backend

# Scoring

Score each field with additive weighted rules to produce a confidence score (0–1).

+5 if type=email

+4 if autocomplete=email

+3 if name|id|class matches /\b(e-?mail|mail)\b/i

+2 if label/placeholder contains “email” or includes @

+1 if pattern contains @ or TLDs (.com, .edu, etc.)

−2 if label contains just “username” (track separately as username-ish)

−3 if field is hidden/readonly/offscreen

# False Positive Control

Keep email vs username as separate labels. Some apps accept both in one box; that’s fine—expose both labels with confidence.

title: Save Every Registered Wallet
V1: Backfill and validate historical permit payouts (GitHub + on-chain)
body:
## Goals

- Recover historical permit data from GitHub issues and comments.
- Rebuild permits into the current schema and de-duplicate against the database.
- Validate remaining permits against on-chain activity on Ethereum and Gnosis.
- Produce a final report of matched, withdrawn, and unresolved permits.
- Improve the foundation of the XP system
- have near complete auditability with 1:1 ratio of `issue label totals == stored permit totals`, or at the very least, each task having verified/tracked payouts

***

## Scope

### 1. Scrape and reconstruct permits

- Enumerate all Ubiquity-owned GitHub orgs and repositories.
- For each issue:
    - Filter comments created by the `prod` & `dev` UbiquityOS.
    - Extract any base64-encoded permit URLs from comment bodies.
    - Decode the base64 payloads and rebuild permit objects into the current expected shape.
- Exclude any permits that already exist in the production database.


### 2. Ad-hoc / manual permits

- In addition to bot comments, include comments by:
    - `@0x4007` for manually sent claim URLs when the bot was down or broken (personally happened to me).
    - `@gentlementlegen` where claim URLs may have been copy-pasted manually when things were down/broken (I'm positive I saw it happen for another contributor, if not myself).
- Parse and process these comments for claim URLs using the same pipeline as bot comments.
- Treat these as best-effort coverage to improve audit completeness.


### 3. Permit validity checks

- For all reconstructed permits not already in the DB:
    - Check on-chain whether the permit nonce has been invalidated.
        - Case A: The permit was claimed by the `beneficiary`.
        - Case B: The signer invalidated/withdrew the permit via the `owner` address.
- If claimed:
    - Match the permit directly to an on-chain transaction involving the `beneficiary`.
- If not claimed:
    - Attempt to locate the invalidation transaction from the `owner` address; otherwise classify as “assumed withdrawn”.

***

## On-chain validation (Ethereum + Gnosis)

Both options require mapping `beneficiary` addresses to users in the production DB.

### Common requirement

- Map `beneficiary` → user by:
    - Using the current wallet mapping in the production DB where possible.
    - Where mappings have changed, parse the `username` from the original bot permit comment to resolve historical ownership.


### Option A: CSV-based, thresholded

- Group reconstructed permits by `beneficiary` address and sum total amounts.
- Exclude addresses with a total under a configurable threshold (e.g. 1,000 USD equivalent).
- For remaining addresses:
    - Manually export transaction history CSVs from Etherscan and GnosisScan.
    - Parse CSVs and group transfers that match `permit transfer from` patterns from known funding wallets.
- Accept that low-earning contributors below the threshold may remain unresolved.


### Option B: Programmatic, full coverage

- Build a structure such as `Record<IssueUrl, Array<{ ...Permit, txHash }>>`.
- For each distinct wallet address:
    - Page through full transaction history from RPC / explorer APIs.
    - Attempt to match permit parameters to on-chain call arguments or transfer patterns.
- For permits without an associated transaction hash:
    - Group them by contributor and issue.
    - Enforce that each contributor can only successfully claim once per issue.
    - Write leftover unmatched permits to a file for manual inspection.
- Store matched permits (with tx hash) keyed by issue/repo/org.

***

## Scale / complexity

- Expected scale: thousands of transactions and hundreds of missing permits.
- Non-trivial data volume and debugging effort across:
    - GitHub API scraping and parsing.
    - Base64 decoding and schema normalization.
    - On-chain history queries on two networks.
    - Heuristic matching and manual review for edge cases.

- A traditional button on the main website to sign up/login
- Comment on top of the page that only trial accounts with limited task number are currently available
- Input name, email, verify email with the code

- We check the submitted info internally, see if we want to approve them or not

   *limiting number of new tasks will reduce requirements for customer support
   *this way, we accumulate small traction with different kinds of businesses and test/improve the system with minimal resources
   *good to test the system before committing to large organizations like SKY/etc cuz they are gonna want to see traction/proof of efficiency for potential partner project that were not supported/developed internally

title: Cron embedding queue exceeds Voyage token limit but workflow still succeeds
body:
## Summary
The cron workflow can succeed while the embedding queue silently aborts when a single Voyage batch exceeds the model token limit.

On April 8, 2026, the `Cron` workflow run below completed with a green check, but step 7 (`Run CRON job`) logged a Voyage 400 because one submitted batch was too large. After that error, `src/cron/index.ts` returns early when the queue is enabled, so pending embeddings are left unprocessed and the rest of the cron reprocess pass is skipped.

Run: https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/text-vector-embeddings/actions/runs/24140827510
Job: https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/text-vector-embeddings/actions/runs/24140827510/job/70441428300#step:7:18
Branch: `issue-17-deno-deploy-workflow`
Commit: `834bb5db52a327ce4f4553621cc34477d7f74adf`

## Actual behavior
- `cron.yml` hardcodes `EMBEDDINGS_QUEUE_BATCH_SIZE: "200"` for the Actions cron job.
- `processPendingEmbeddings()` loads up to `batchSize` rows and sends every cleaned document in that set to Voyage in one `embed()` call.
- Voyage rejects the request because the combined batch exceeds the model token budget.
- The error is logged as `Embedding queue failed`, but the cron entrypoint returns instead of failing the job, so the workflow still reports success.

## Expected behavior
- The queue should respect Voyage's per-request token limit, not just a row-count limit.
- Oversized batches should be split and retried automatically, or the job should fail loudly instead of succeeding after skipping work.
- Cron and deployed runtime defaults should not diverge in a way that makes the GitHub Actions queue substantially more aggressive than the deployed worker.

## Likely root cause
- `.github/workflows/cron.yml` uses a fixed batch size of `200`.
- `.github/workflows/update-configuration.yml` uses `EMBEDDINGS_QUEUE_BATCH_SIZE: ${{ secrets.EMBEDDINGS_QUEUE_BATCH_SIZE || '50' }}`, so the deployed runtime defaults are safer than the cron workflow defaults.
- `src/cron/embedding-queue.ts` batches by document count only; it does not estimate or cap tokens before calling Voyage.
- `src/cron/index.ts` catches non-rate-limit queue errors and returns early while the workflow remains green.

## Impact
- Pending documents remain without embeddings.
- The hourly cron reprocess pass is skipped after the queue error.
- Maintainers can miss the regression because the workflow is marked successful.

## Acceptance criteria
- Embedding batches are split by a safe token budget (or dynamically shrunk on Voyage 400 token-limit responses), not only by document count.
- Token-limit failures do not silently short-circuit the cron run while the job still passes.
- The cron workflow and deployed worker use aligned, configurable queue defaults.
- Regression tests cover an oversized mixed-length batch that would previously exceed Voyage's token cap.

title: Codebase semantic search
body:
For on boarding new developers, or just to synchronize existing developers, we should be generating embeddings of our code base. We can do per file or on the function level, depending on which has better performance.

I asked GPT for the best sorting method on the [embedding leaderboard](https://huggingface.co/spaces/mteb/leaderboard). 

Later it clarified that we should be sorting by "retrieval with instructions" for best results. 

[FollowIR-7B](https://huggingface.co/jhu-clsp/FollowIR-7B) is the highest ranked. 

We should be doing this in two steps:
1. Primarily, we should be generating embeddings of the new files when pull requests are merged.
2. We should have a tool that we can run manually (manual dispatch on GitHub actions ok) to generate all the embeddings. This would be expected to be used if there were pushes directly to the default branch and were not added via pull request

### additional context

> For this use case (codebase question-answering), your focus should be on retrieval tasks. Based on the criteria provided, here’s how I would prioritize the metrics:

> 1. **Retrieval Average (15 datasets)**: This should be your highest priority. The better the retrieval capability of the model, the more relevant code chunks it will retrieve when you ask a question about the codebase.

> 2. **Embedding Dimensions**: A higher embedding dimension may provide more nuanced representations of code and questions, improving retrieval accuracy. However, this needs to be balanced with memory usage and model size.

> 3. **Model Size (Million Parameters)**: Larger models tend to perform better in generating high-quality embeddings, but at the cost of memory and speed. Consider how much memory and computational power you can afford.

> 4. **Max Tokens**: A higher max token limit is useful for code because some functions or files can be quite large. You'll want a model that can handle bigger chunks of code.

> 5. **Classification Average (12 datasets)**: Code-related tasks sometimes involve classification (e.g., determining the type of question or identifying sections of code). A higher classification score can help in such scenarios.

> 6. **STS Average (10 datasets)**: Semantic Textual Similarity (STS) is also important as it measures how well the embeddings capture semantic meaning, which is useful for understanding the context and retrieving the right code section.

> ### Sorting Criteria:
> Sort by **Retrieval Average** first, then consider **Max Tokens** and **Embedding Dimensions** for practical handling of code and performance optimization.

> The other metrics like **Classification**, **Clustering**, and **Reranking** are less critical for your specific use case, but they can help refine the quality if you have a secondary need for such tasks.

title: Accept the ai.ubq.fi #1155 interface change in the VPS release bridge
body:
ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi#1155, which fixes ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi#1125, was merged as [`2de00a80`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/2de00a80f812901680bd6e1109e90fbc7f0dac24). It changes the bridge-facing interface of ai.ubq.fi's VPS metrics modules again, on top of the #1027 changes that #150 tracks. #150 does not cover these changes.

## What changed

| | Before #1155 (ai.ubq.fi `36503598`, which already includes #1027) | After #1155 (`2de00a80`) |
|---|---|---|
| journalctl argv built by `createVpsJournalReader(...).read` ([`ops/vps-journal-reader.ts:20`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/2de00a80f812901680bd6e1109e90fbc7f0dac24/ops/vps-journal-reader.ts#L20)) | 5 arguments: `["--unit=ai-ubq-fi.service", "--since=@<s>", "--until=@<s>", "--output=json", "--no-pager"]` | 6 arguments: `["--unit=ai-ubq-fi.service", "--since=@<s>", "--until=@<s>", "--output=json", "--all", "--no-pager"]` |
| Trusted argv check in `runVpsJournalCommand(args, limits, cwd)` ([`ops/vps-journal-reader.ts:101-111`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/2de00a80f812901680bd6e1109e90fbc7f0dac24/ops/vps-journal-reader.ts#L101-L111)) | accepts only the 5-argument shape | accepts only the 6-argument shape: `args.length === 6`, `args[4] === "--all"`, `args[5] === "--no-pager"`. Anything else throws "VPS journal command refused". |
| `createVpsJoinFileStorage` ([`ops/vps-metrics-storage.ts:36-45`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/2de00a80f812901680bd6e1109e90fbc7f0dac24/ops/vps-metrics-storage.ts#L36-L45)) | `(root, policy, cipher, current, now = Date.now)` | `(root, policy, cipher, current, now = Date.now, stateReadMs = VPS_METRICS_STATE_READ_MS)`. `VPS_METRICS_STATE_READ_MS` is 10 s, and the value must be a positive safe integer. It bounds the one release-state read made under the deploy lock, and a read that exceeds it refuses the save. |
| Checkpoint files in `.data/sentinel-vps-metrics` | a save removes only its own temporary file | each save, under the deploy lock, deletes stray temporaries and checkpoints whose mtime is older than `policy.evidenceMaxAgeMs`. So every bridge that shares the directory must use the same retention. |
| Join checkpoint ([`ops/vps-metrics-types.ts:98`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/2de00a80f812901680bd6e1109e90fbc7f0dac24/ops/vps-metrics-types.ts#L98)) | `schema: 1` | `schema: 2`. Schema-1 checkpoints are refused and not migrated. The binding digest schema is unchanged. |

`runVpsJournalCommand` is still re-exported `@public` from `ops/vps-release-metrics.ts:35` for the bridge to compose its journal reader.

## Sentinel files involved

None of these files builds or checks the journalctl argv itself, and none calls `runVpsJournalCommand` or `createVpsJoinFileStorage` directly. I checked with `git grep` on both refs below. The argv is built inside ai.ubq.fi's reader and handed to whatever implements `host.journalCommand`.

- On `development` (`87e28fd4`), `src/host/vps-release.ts:58-75` (the `MetricsModule` interface) and `:267-319` (the composition) still use the pre-#1027 interface. They pass the driver's `runVpsCommand(program, args, cwd)` to `createVpsJournalReader` and construct `VpsJournalMetrics` with 5 arguments. #150 tracks that.
- On the #150 branch `origin/codex/master-plan-gfa795549e5` (`8e34ff6f`), not yet merged:
  - `src/host/vps-release.ts:77-95` and `:406-433` pass `options.journalCommand` straight into `createVpsJournalReader`, and pass `options.joinStorage` as the metrics `storage`.
  - `src/release/vps-metrics.ts:35-51` defines the `VpsJoinStorage` and `VpsBoundedJournalCommand` types.
  - `src/host/release-bridge.ts:633-650` and `:683-706` take both from `ReleaseBridgeCapabilities.host`.
  - `ops/vps-release-bridge.ts:50-72` loads that host from the owner-installed, hash-pinned capabilities module (`RELEASE_BRIDGE_CAPABILITIES`).
  - Tests stub both: `tests/host/release-bridge-metrics_test.ts:88-107` and `tests/host/vps-release-host_test.ts:47-55`.

## Impact

Nothing is broken live today. `sentinel-release` is disabled, and the bridge's pinned driver predates #1027 (`21e4a2a9`, per ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi#1146).

Once the driver is re-pinned at or after `2de00a80`, these are the risks:
- **Journal command.** Suppose `host.journalCommand` is not the pinned tree's own `runVpsJournalCommand`, for example a copy of the #1027 five-argument check, or a function taken from an older tree. Then every journal read is refused, every sample comes back `coverage_missing`, and every VPS release is refused.
- **Storage.** A capabilities module that calls `createVpsJoinFileStorage` with five arguments keeps working, because the sixth is optional.
- **Old checkpoints.** A schema-1 checkpoint left by a #1027 driver would be refused. None should exist, because no #1027 driver has run under the bridge.

## Acceptance

- `host.journalCommand` is the pinned driver tree's `runVpsJournalCommand`. If the capabilities module validates the argv itself, it accepts exactly the 6-argument `--all` shape above.
- The capabilities module either passes `stateReadMs` to `createVpsJoinFileStorage` or accepts the 10 s default. It uses one `evidenceMaxAgeMs` for every bridge that shares `.data/sentinel-vps-metrics`.
- The interface pin test asked for in #150 also covers the journalctl argv shape and the checkpoint schema, so a mismatch fails CI instead of failing at release time.
- Land this together with #150. Do not re-pin the driver at or past `2de00a80` until both are done.

The cutoff rule shipped because the fixed list could not cover the records in flight at install (645, 646, 657, 663, 1140).

**Failure scenario.**

- **(2)** A spent record at `work` with head null is not ready, but the diagnostic explains it as ready (null). So `notReadyByReason` undercounts and gives no reason.

- **(2)** Add a `review_rounds_spent` reason to `explainMatrixNotReady`, using `reviewRoundsLeft` with the planning run's cutoff.
- **(3)** Record the owner's answer in DECISIONS once it is given.
- Add a test that every CI-first runtime is also in the CI-correction, conflict-resolution and refresh re-arm allowlists and in `LEGACY_REVIEW_CUTOFF.revisions`, so future pins keep the set together.

**Severity.** P3.

title: Protect the remaining merge-authority files and check target protected paths at merge time
body:
Follow-up from the generation-80 reviews. Code references are at R80 `d5cc84402` on `development`.

**Problem.**
1. **Merge-authority files are outside `protectedPaths`.** Generation 80's merge guarantees still depend on files that are not in `protectedPaths` (src/host/local-config.ts:95; the generation-80 block is at :300-316). Each of these was confirmed unprotected at d5cc84402:
   - ops/hosted-autonomy-delivery.ts: `boundReviewReceipts` (:39), `authorizingReceipt` (:75), `baseAndHeadAreMerged` (:171), `verifiedMergedDelivery` (:185) and `buildHostedReleaseRequest` (:208).
   - ops/hosted-autonomy-runner.ts: runs the delivery pass (:77) and the follow-up pass (:112).
   - ops/hosted-autonomy-scopes.ts: `readTip` (:62), the uncached tip re-read that the off-tip guarantee relies on.
   - src/repair/review-gate.ts: `taskAcceptanceRefusal` (:77) and `reviewAuthorizesMerge` (:193), the shared predicate that refuses an unresolved P0/P1.
   - src/repair/transitions.ts: `markBlocked` (:619), used for every park, including the off-tip park.
   - src/github/git-executor.ts: the git runner behind the runtime's carried patch proof.
   - src/repair/vps-delivery.ts: `gatewayRequestBindsDelivery` (:30), checked before every Gateway merge.
2. **No protected-path check at merge time.** `preMergeGate` (ops/hosted-autonomy-spent-delivery.ts:423-478) and `carriedMergeGate` (:818-878) never compare the PR's files with the target's protected paths. They rely on the runtime's check at publication time, and some spent candidates were published before a7667209e gave ai.ubq.fi its protected paths.
3. **Held CI runs are approved before any review.** Under CI first, the launcher approves GitHub-held CI runs for model-authored heads that no review has seen (`ciFirstApprovalEligible`, ops/hosted-autonomy-delivery-pass.ts:87). The trade-off is not recorded.

**Failure scenario.**
- **(1)** A model-authored Sentinel candidate makes `readTip` return a pass-cached value, loosens `baseAndHeadAreMerged`, or weakens `reviewAuthorizesMerge`. Protected-path admission does not refuse it, so it reaches review and CI as an ordinary candidate. Once promoted, the launcher can merge outside the closed shapes. This is defence in depth only: the live launcher runs from the owner-promoted sentinel-supervisor branch.
- **(2)** A legacy spent candidate that edits a path now protected on the Gateway merges once its head turns green. The 17 live spent PRs were checked, and none touches a Gateway protected path today.
- **(3)** Today both pull_request workflows run with `permissions: contents: read` and reference no secrets: ai.ubq.fi "Gateway CI" (.github/workflows/deno-deploy.yml) and sentinel .github/workflows/ci.yml. If either workflow later gains a secret or a write permission, model-written code would run with it before any review.

**Suggested fix.**
- **(1)** Add these files to `protectedPaths` and to the protected-path pin test in tests/repair/ci-first-round-cap_test.ts (:373-397).
- **(2)** Before a spent or carried merge, list the PR's files and refuse `protected_path` on any match with `selectTrustedTargetPolicyV1(...).protectedPaths` (src/host/target-policy.ts:70).
- **(3)** Record the trade-off in docs/DECISIONS.md. Make approval refuse, or add a failing check, when the target's pull_request workflow references `secrets.` or requests a write permission.

**Severity.** P3. These are defence-in-depth gaps with no live exposure today.

title: Review follow-up filing: file off-tip carried merges, dedupe by PR, prove the listing horizon, anchor the window
body:
Follow-up from the generation-80 reviews. Code references are at R80 `d5cc84402` on `development`.

**Problem and failure scenarios.** The owner rule says a merged PR's unresolved P2/P3 findings are filed as new issues. The filing can skip or duplicate them:

1. **An off-tip carried merge loses its follow-up** (generation-81 follow-up).
   - On the Gateway, a carried merge that landed off its tip is parked, and no production request is written (ops/hosted-autonomy-delivery-pass.ts:442-484).
   - `planFollowUpCandidates` reads only production requests (ops/hosted-autonomy-follow-ups.ts:126-133), so the merged PR's P2/P3 findings are never filed.
2. **De-duplication is keyed on the receipt.**
   - `markerNamesCandidate` matches (repository, PR, receipt id) (follow-ups.ts:94-103), while the module doc (:13) and DECISIONS say nothing is filed twice.
   - Scenario: a follow-up is filed against receipt X. Then a newer clean P2/P3 receipt Y appears on the same PR, head and base: for example, from a review in flight when the delivery pass merged a `review`-step record, or from a missing-acceptance re-review. A second issue is filed and becomes another admitted, charged Sentinel task.
3. **The listing horizon is capped.**
   - The pass lists back to the repository's oldest candidate with at most 5 pages (ops/hosted-autonomy-follow-up-pass.ts:111-138; follow-ups.ts:42-43). Candidates are processed oldest first (follow-ups.ts:134-136).
   - Once more than 500 issues and PRs are created inside the window, every candidate reports `listing_unproven` and filing stops silently.
   - Today about 100 are created per 37 hours. The planned matrix scale-up toward 256 concurrent cells would pass the cap.
4. **The window is anchored at now.**
   - `from = max(epoch, now - 72h)` (follow-ups.ts:127). The live launcher does not run the follow-up pass yet.
   - A merged PR whose request is more than 72 hours old when the generation-80 launcher first runs is never filed. PRs 1105 and 1052 (requests at 2026-10-16T11:50Z and 12:40Z) age out at about 2026-10-19T11:50Z.
5. **Depth 3 is never filed.**
   - `FOLLOW_UP_MAX_DEPTH` is 2 (follow-ups.ts:53-54), and `depth_exhausted` (follow-up-pass.ts:189-192) drops depth-3 findings silently.
   - The owner rule has no depth limit, and the cap has no sign-off.

**Suggested fix.**
- **(1)** Let the follow-up pass take an off-tip park (merged by the App, merge sha in the park message) as a source, keyed by PR and merge sha, so its findings are filed once.
- **(2)** In `markerNamesCandidate`, treat any App-authored marker with the same repository and PR as already filed, whatever its receipt or depth. Add a test with a second receipt.
- **(3)** Process candidates newest first. Treat the listing as proven back to its oldest item, and decide only the candidates inside that horizon; report only the older ones as unproven.
- **(4)** Anchor the window at max(launcher activation, request time), or start it at the epoch for passes before the first successful one.
- **(5)** Get owner sign-off on the depth cap, or file depth-3 findings under an opt-out label so Sentinel does not repair them.

**Severity.** P3. Item (4) is time-sensitive until the generation-80 launcher is installed.

title: Carried and spent delivery: book only exact-tip merges, tighten carried waits and proofs, trim the spent read window
body:
Follow-up from the generation-80 reviews. Code references are at R80 `d5cc84402` on `development`.

**Problem and failure scenarios.**

1. **Non-carried merges can be booked off the tip.**
   - The delivery pass re-reads the tip uncached right before the merge (ops/hosted-autonomy-delivery-pass.ts:369-383), but GitHub has no compare-and-swap on the base.
   - A merge made in this pass is booked through `baseAndHeadAreMerged` (delivery-pass.ts:485-490; ops/hosted-autonomy-delivery.ts:171-183). That check accepts any first parent that is a proven descendant of the reviewed base. Only carried merges require parents exactly [T, H1] (:442-446).
   - Scenario: the tip re-read for an exact-base merge returns B, then an owner merge lands before the PUT. GitHub creates merge(B', H), a tree no CI ran on, and the pass books it as a delivery with a release request.
2. **A self carried merge that lands off its tip lingers.**
   - The pass reports `carried_merged_off_tip`, then `if (!gateway) continue` (delivery-pass.ts:452).
   - The record stays at `work` with an `unavailable` wait for the launcher's record (src/repair/loop-carried-delivery.ts:604-612). It keeps holding the sentinel delivery line for about 12 polls, roughly 2.4 hours at live cadence.
   - Each pass re-proves it through the adoption path (`adoptableSpentMerge` plus `carriedPatchRefusal` at :407-426): 2 compares, 2 git/commits reads, 4 recursive trees and 2 rendered diffs. All of that runs before the cheap parents check at :442.
   - After 6 hours it parks with the generic "the carried delivery stalled for 6 hours: merged without the launcher's delivery record", which does not name the off-tip cause.
3. **Any `unavailable` wait counts as awaited.**
   - `carriedRecordAwaited` (ops/hosted-autonomy-spent-delivery.ts:607-610) treats any `unavailable` wait at `work` as awaited by the launcher. The runtime also writes that wait before any merge, for "patch proof <kind>" (loop-carried-delivery.ts:375) and for "the pull request still reports <old head>" (:418).
   - The window exemption (`spentReadWindow`, spent-delivery.ts:509-524) then reads that record's task and pull on every pass for up to 6 hours, only to report `carried_awaiting_runtime`.
4. **The runtime proof misses mode-only paths.**
   - A mode-only change prints no index line, so equal patch bytes do not bind that path's content (src/github/git-carried-patch.ts:14-20 and the arguments at :70-100).
   - Scenario: a PR runs chmod +x on s.sh, the base later changes s.sh's content, and the refresh merges cleanly. Both patches read only "old mode 100644 / new mode 100755", so the runtime proof holds and writes the marker.
   - The launcher's tree proof compares old blob ids (ops/hosted-autonomy-github-trees.ts) and refuses, so nothing unsafe merges. But the record holds the marker and the delivery line until the 6-hour stall park.
   - DECISIONS ("Full blob ids on every index line make equal bytes mean equal contents ... modes") overstates the runtime proof.
5. **A red H1 is refreshed again before its CI is read.**
   - `executeCarriedDelivery` calls `ensureBaseRefreshIntent` (loop-carried-delivery.ts:423-438) before `readChecks` (:440).
   - If the base moves before R80 sees H1's red CI, H1 is refreshed to H2 instead of parking `...the refreshed head's required CI failed`. That can repeat up to `CARRIED_REFRESH_LIMIT` (6, :114) times. Each repeat is a fresh CI run, made while the record holds its repository's delivery line.
6. **The spent read window spends slots on records that can only end `base_moved`.**
   - With D3 off, `spentReadWindow` (spent-delivery.ts:496-540) still admits parked spent records whose base is behind the tip.
   - Each one costs `readTrustedTask` and `readPull` (delivery-pass.ts:227-231 and :265) before `preMergeGate` refuses it `base_moved` (spent-delivery.ts:440-447).
   - Live, all 26 to 36 CI-red spent records were behind the tip, so a deliverable exact-base park gets one of the 8 slots only about 8/N of the time.

**Suggested fix.**
- **(1)** For `mergedThisPass`, book only when the merge commit's parents are exactly [re-read tip, head]. Otherwise report `delivery:<id>:merged_off_tip:sha=...` and write nothing. Keep `baseAndHeadAreMerged` for adopting merges made outside this pass. Alternatively, merge by an atomic fast-forward-only ref update of a commit with parents [T, H].
- **(2)** Check `pull.parents` against [base, head] before `carriedPatchRefusal` in the adoption path. Let the runtime check the parents itself, so a self off-tip merge stops holding the line and parks with an off-tip message.
- **(3)** Exempt an `unavailable` wait only when the last-known pull is merged, or correct the commit and DECISIONS wording.
- **(4)** Also hash `git diff --raw --no-abbrev -z --no-renames <merge-base> <head>` together with the patch bytes, so the runtime and launcher proofs agree. Correct the DECISIONS sentence.
- **(5)** Read H1's checks first. Park on a candidate-caused red, and refresh only a green or pending H1.
- **(6)** Read the tip once before building the window. While D3 is off, leave out records whose base is not that tip; the carried exemption already covers carried heads on a moved base.

Add a regression test for each.

**Severity.** P3. Items (1) and (2) need a race of under a second. Items (3) to (6) affect cost and precision; none merges anything unsafe.

title: Give spent and legacy records an exit from the review ceiling's silent dead ends
body:
Follow-up from the generation-80 reviews. Code references are at R80 `d5cc84402` on `development`.

**Problem.** Several states at the review-round ceiling never resolve and report nothing.

1. **The legacy base-red hold has no exit** (generation-81 follow-up).
   - Take a legacy record with its final round open, at the ceiling on a moved base, whose head is red because its reviewed base B0 is red, still pending past its bound, or unattributed. It is parked `CI checks failed without base evidence: ...` (src/repair/loop-carried-delivery.ts:214-219 calls `holdUncorrectableLegacyHead` at :273-300).
   - B0 is fixed and stays red, so the head never turns green. The correction rule matches only `CI checks failed: `, the flake re-run needs base == tip, and `legacyReviewRoundClassDrift` stays silent because the final round is still open.
   - For base_red the message is also wrong, because base evidence exists.
   - docs/DECISIONS.md says the record is "re-admitted only by the green rule", which can never fire.
2. **A no-verdict attempt spends the legacy final round.**
   - The final round is open only while no review was admitted at or after the cutoff, and an ambiguous (no-verdict) admission counts (src/repair/review-round-cap.ts:273-292).
   - `recoverFromNoVerdictReview` re-requests (src/repair/loop-review-request.ts:466-479), and the ceiling gate then parks the record UNREVIEWED. The exception is spent, no review ever completed, and the CI fix was already charged.
3. **Review intents that defer forever.** The ceiling gate defers whenever an intent is in flight (src/repair/loop-review-round-cap.ts:65-70). Two paths never clear the intent:
   - With counter 0 and ledger at 3 or more, `observeReview`'s counting branch needs `reviewRounds >= 1` (src/repair/loop-review-observation.ts:187-206). `recoverFromNoVerdictReview` then forwards the record with its `review_request` intent still set (loop-review-request.ts:478), so every run defers.
   - The `reviewRounds + 1` intent with no exact bound journal defers without a write on every run (loop-review-observation.ts:187-201).
4. **Some CI-fix budgets start already spent.**
   - CI fixes are counted in `counters.retries` (src/repair/ci-first-policy.ts:97-99), and the rollback note (:15-19) says no R79 path writes that counter.
   - Live rows still carry values from older generations, so these records begin generation 80 with fixes already used.

**Failure scenario.**
- **(1)** This is not live: round 3 found 33 of 36 legacy heads attributing to the candidate, and 3 green. It appears as soon as a legacy head is refreshed or fixed while `development` is red. That record then sits blocked for good, with no report.
- **(2)** Since 2026-10-16T08Z, outside 684, there were 179 `review_request` charges against about 143 completed receipts, so roughly 20% of attempts give no verdict. About one legacy record in five loses its owner-granted final review this way.
- **(3)** A record shaped like 264 (counter 0, ledger 3) reads its pull request and defers forever; none is live. Live 647 (PR 1011, counter 3, ledger 4) has deferred without a write since 2026-10-14T00:12Z under R79 and R80. It costs a PR read every run.
- **(4)** At state 719d8f30d, issue-ubiquity-sentinel-61 has retries 3. Once re-admitted, it parks `CI fix attempts exhausted (3 of 3)` without a single fix. sentinel-76 (retries 2) gets 1 fix, and sentinel-21 (retries 1) gets 2.

**Suggested fix.**
- **(1)** Send a base-red or unattributed legacy head on a moved base through an uncharged mechanical refresh onto a green tip, then its CI fix and its one final round. At minimum, use a distinct base-red park message, report these records every pass (for example `retry:<id>:denied:legacy_base_red`), and reword DECISIONS to "parks until the owner acts".
- **(2)** For a legacy record, count the final round as spent only once a review has completed, or allow exactly one no-verdict re-request. Keep the hard cap for ordinary records and document the choice.
- **(3)** At the ceiling, when the in-flight intent is a `review_request` whose journal has concluded, or one with no bound journal past a bound (6 hours, like the other ceiling waits), clear it the way `recoverExpiredReviewAttempt` does and park with a precise blocker. Add tests for the 264 and 647 shapes.
- **(4)** Count only `retry` charges admitted after the CI-first runtime's activation, or record that these rows start with fixes already spent and correct the comment.

**Severity.** P3. Only 647 is live, and it blocks no one.

title: Treat required CI as green only when every expected check exists and the listing was actually read
body:
Follow-up from the generation-80 reviews. Code references are at R80 `d5cc84402` on `development`.

**Problem.**
- **Only existing checks count.** `decideCiGate` (src/repair/loop-checks.ts:22-42) returns `proceed` when every check run that exists is completed and successful. It never compares them with the checks the workflow will produce. Three places rely on it:
  - the CI-first review gate (src/repair/loop-ci-first.ts:231-232);
  - the ceiling's moved-base read (src/repair/loop-carried-delivery.ts:196);
  - the carried step (loop-carried-delivery.ts:440-444), which then writes the carried-merge marker.
- **The launcher has the same rule.** `hasAllChecksGreen` (ops/hosted-autonomy-github.ts:213-228) is used by `headIsGreen` (ops/hosted-autonomy-spent-delivery.ts:286-298) for every launcher merge, and by `carriedMergeGate` (:842-844). No review sits between H1 turning green and the carried merge.
- **ai.ubq.fi creates a required check late.** `verify-artifact` has `needs: [validate, mac-containment, darwin-native]` (Gateway CI, .github/workflows/deno-deploy.yml), so it has no check run until those jobs finish.
- **An unreadable listing reads as red.** `hasAllChecksGreen` returns false, not an error, when the listing is unreadable (github.ts:214-215). The retry pass's spent CI read (ops/hosted-autonomy-retry-pass.ts:362-370) then records the head in `ciReadHeads` as read and not green.

**Failure scenario.**
- **Gap before verify-artifact.** Observed live: head f0008beb62 had validate completed at 08:41:53Z and verify-artifact started at 08:41:58Z; 383c3ff83e showed a 6-second gap. A CI-first poll in that gap sees 3 of 3 runs green and requests a review before the required verify-artifact job exists. A carried H1 polled in the gap gets the carried-merge marker, and a launcher read in the same window would merge it with verify-artifact never run. The same applies to any job a workflow creates late or only under a condition.
- **Failed listing wastes a correction slot.** A rate-limited or 5xx check-run listing for green legacy 618 gives `green=false` and adds the head to `ciReadHeads`. If its re-run is settled, the head is planned as a CI correction (`other:CI checks failed:`) and takes one of the 4 correction slots per pass. R80 then reads it green and delivers it.

**Suggested fix.**
- Require the head's latest check names to cover the check names of the base it is tested against: the reviewed base for the CI-first gate, the tip T for a carried head. Both are already read on the failure paths. Alternatively, require the head's workflow run or check suite to be completed.
- Apply this in `decideCiGate`'s callers and in the launcher's `hasAllChecksGreen`.
- Give the launcher a tri-state read (green, not green, unreadable), and add a head to `ciReadHeads` only after a successful, non-empty listing.
- Add tests: a head with 3 of 4 expected check names waits, and an unreadable listing plans nothing.

**Severity.** P3. A red-CI head is not merged today, but a required job that has not started yet can be skipped.

title: Generation 81: open the hosted CI-fix route and re-admit pre-review CI parks on a moved base
body:
Follow-up from the generation-80 reviews. Code references are at R80 `d5cc84402` on `development`.

**Problem.** In hosted generation 80, any red head that has no completed review of its own parks with no way out:

That covers new candidates and also the refreshed head of every already-reviewed record whose base moved.
- **Moved base blocks re-admission.** The launcher's re-run and green rules re-admit a pre-review park only while its base is still the tip (ops/hosted-autonomy-retry-pass.ts:358-361; ops/hosted-autonomy-ci-rerun.ts:179-182 and :252). ai.ubq.fi `development` moves 16-25 times a day and the pending park waits 6 hours, so a park almost always outlives its base. A head that later turns green on a moved base stays parked.
- **Exhausted park gets nothing.** `CI fix attempts exhausted (3 of 3): ...` (ci-first-policy.ts:79-80, written at loop-ci-first.ts:161-167) is not in `CI_PRE_REVIEW_PARK_PREFIXES` (ci-first-policy.ts:91-94), so it gets no free flake re-run either.
- **Misleading test comment.** tests/host/hosted-autonomy-ci-first_test.ts:177 says "the runtime's freshness gate owns it", but the runtime skips blocked records.

**Failure scenario.**
- At the integration review (sequence 38661), refreshed heads of reviewed records failed validate on prettier and eslint drift: 645, 646, 649 and 1128 onto 2756425c16, and 583, 615, 617, 629 and 633 onto 973bb2f and ded498f.
- Under R79 each of those was reviewed and then CI-corrected. Under hosted R80 each parks `CI red before review; awaiting a CI fix`, and `planHostedRetries` returns [] under every runtime (tests/repair/ci-first-refresh-red_test.ts pins this).

**Suggested fix.** In generation 81, once R80 is healthy and can serve as its rollback target:
- Set `HOSTED_PRE_REVIEW_CI_FIXES` true in the new runtime and pin it in `HOSTED_AUTONOMY_CI_FIRST_FIX_RUNTIMES`, so the fix rule re-admits red pre-review parks through the CI fix marker.
- Under a proven CI-first runtime, return a pre-review park on a moved base to `work`. The refresh is deterministic and uncharged, and the runtime gates CI before review. Keep the unchanged-base condition only for the any-runtime green rule.
- Let the once-per-head re-run and the green rule apply to the exhausted park.
- Fix the test comment.

docs/DECISIONS.md ("Generation 80 CI-first pipeline") accepts this for generation 80 as a generation-81 follow-up.

**Severity.** P2 (liveness). Most red heads in the hosted queue stall until generation 81. Nothing unsafe happens.

title: Bind carried deliveries in release acceptance and issue closure before sentinel-release is enabled
body:
Follow-up from the generation-80 reviews. Code references are at R80 `d5cc84402` on `development`.

**Problem.** A carried merge works like this: a spent record whose head H0 was reviewed on base B0 is mechanically refreshed to H1 on tip T, and the launcher merges H1 under H0's review. The merge is booked with a production release request that names H0's receipt and gives H1/T as its source (`carriedRequestBindsDelivery`, ops/hosted-autonomy-spent-delivery.ts:640). Every binder on the release path still requires the receipt to name the record's own head and base, so a carried delivery can never be accepted or closed:

- `gatewayRequestBindsDelivery` requires `review.pullRequest.head === record.target.head` and the same base (src/repair/vps-delivery.ts:53-54). The runtime's release observation uses it (`observeGatewayVpsDelivery`, src/repair/loop-release.ts:284), and so does the launcher's closure gate (ops/hosted-autonomy-closure-pass.ts:61).
- For the self scope, `acceptRelease` calls `deliveryTaskRefusal` (src/repair/loop-release.ts:213, src/repair/loop-task-context.ts:318-338). Its `authorizingReceipt` needs the exact head, so the merged record is blocked with `MERGE_WITHOUT_REVIEW_DETAIL` (missing_evidence).
- R79 answers the same way.

**Failure scenario.**
- The launcher carries an ai.ubq.fi record and books it at `delivery` beside its request.
- Once sentinel-release is enabled again and the VPS release is accepted, `observeGatewayVpsDelivery` answers `wait` on every run before it reads any release state. The record never reaches `done`, its `unavailable` wait re-arms forever, and the closure pass never closes it.
- A carried sentinel self delivery whose release is accepted is blocked "merge without review", even though it merged under a proven carried review.

A round-2 recheck probe showed `carriedRequestBindsDelivery` true, `gatewayRequestBindsDelivery` false, and 0 release-state reads. Today the source issue still closes through the PR body's `Resolves #N`; this was verified for ai.ubq.fi 600, 664, 684 and 688. The record, though, stays in `delivery` beside its open request.

**Suggested fix.**
- Give the runtime and launcher binders a carried variant. It accepts a request whose receipt is `carriedRequestReceipt` (a completed, clean App review of an earlier head of the same PR) only after it re-derives the patch proof between the receipt's H0/B0 and the request's H1/T. Use the runtime's git proof `carriedPatchHolds` or the launcher's tree proof `mergeBaseTreeChanges`, and authorize the task as of `reviewedIdentity(record, receipt)`.
- Use the variant in `observeGatewayVpsDelivery`, in the closure pass and in the self `acceptRelease`.

---

Outcomes:

1. We improve reviewer QOL. They re-assign and don't have to deal with telling the user they need to push a fresh commit or open a new PR.
2. We improve DX by automating the process of pulling in the most recent commits from that branch without them needing to force a commit just to refresh the PR for reviewers.

title: Allow Users to Select and Configure Specific Plugin Branches
body:
Currently, the plugin installer GUI assumes users always want to configure and install the version of a plugin found on a single, predefined branch (initially hardcoded to `development`, later updated to the repository's default branch). However, plugins often have different versions, features, or configuration schemas across various branches (e.g., `main`, `development`, feature branches, release tags).

Users need the ability to explicitly select the desired branch for a plugin they are configuring, and the system must ensure that the correct manifest is used for rendering the UI and the correct identifier (Action reference or URL) is saved in the configuration file.

**Desired Behavior / Acceptance Criteria:**

1.  The configuration editor should display a dropdown allowing users to select from the available branches of the plugin's source repository.
2.  When editing an existing plugin configuration, the dropdown should pre-select the branch specified in the saved configuration identifier (`owner/repo@branch` or parsed from URL).
3.  When editing an existing plugin configuration, the editor UI should initially render based on the manifest fetched from the *configured* branch.
4.  When the user selects a different branch from the dropdown, the editor UI should dynamically update by fetching and rendering the manifest from the newly selected branch.
5.  When saving the configuration, the `plugin` identifier stored in the `uses` array must accurately reflect the user's selected branch:
    *   For Action-based plugins: `owner/repo@selectedBranch`
    *   For URL-based plugins: The correctly transformed URL corresponding to the `selectedBranch` (e.g., `https://...-selected-branch-suffix.domain.com`).
6.  UI elements should be consistent with the rest of the application.
7.  Informational/success toast notifications should auto-dismiss.

## Main issues

We will have problems saving different branches because it is technically correct to have two similar plugins pointing to two different branches. Similarly the plugin would not know we want to change the target branch but will instead stack plugins from different branches together.

title: Follow-up from #1152 (issue #689): test the "Only active" path of the provider bulk buttons
body:
PR #1152 (https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/1152) fixed issue #689. A Codex tier narrowed to individual subscriptions now counts as checked, so "Uncheck shown" works for it. The PR merged in commit 3c12bc88a09fabfb7f948aa242400990c156cc93 (https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/3c12bc88a09fabfb7f948aa242400990c156cc93). This issue holds the one review finding from that PR that is still open on development.

The review found no P0, P1 or P2 problems. The fix itself is correct, including on the path below. The gap is only that no committed test covers that path.

## 1. No test covers the "Only active" filter with a narrowed Codex tier (P3, test coverage)

**Where.** Line numbers are at merge commit 3c12bc88. Both files are unchanged on development b24353e5, so the lines are the same there.

- `tests/admin-capacity-status.test.ts:839`: `providerPicker`, the VM fixture the new tests use.
- `tests/admin-capacity-status.test.ts:865`: `providersOnlyActiveInput: { checked: false }` is hard-coded, so "Only active" is always off.
- `tests/admin-capacity-status.test.ts:867-868`: `providersVisibleEntries` and `providersFilterIsActive` are stubs. The real filter code never runs.
- `tests/admin-capacity-status.test.ts:876-886`: the VM slice list leaves out `renderProvidersPicker`.
- `static/admin.js:9833`: the real `providersVisibleEntries`. With "Only active" on, it keeps the `codex` row when any of its subscriptions is selected (`providerCodexSelection().selected > 0`).
- `static/admin.js:10162`: `renderProvidersPicker`. It recomputes `providersVisibleIds` and calls `updateProvidersStatus`.
- `static/admin.js:10179`: `applyProvidersSelection`. When "Only active" is on, it re-renders through `renderProvidersPicker` instead of patching the rows in place.

**Problem.** The #1152 description says the "Only active" filter caused the same defect as the Codex tier filter. "Only active" can leave a narrowed Codex row as the only row shown, and before the fix "Uncheck shown" was disabled there too. The committed tests (`:891`, `:902`, `:912`) cover only the tier-filter case. They never turn "Only active" on, never run the real visibility filter, and never run the re-render that follows a bulk click with "Only active" on. Nothing else covers it: the only other reference to the control is the element-wiring check in `tests/admin-models-catalog.test.ts:763`.

**Failure scenario.** Someone later changes `providersVisibleEntries` or `renderProvidersPicker`, for example by keeping the Codex row only when `providerSelection.has("codex")`, or by computing `providersVisibleIds` before the counts change. The operator has selected only subscription `sub-a` and turns on "Only active". Then either the narrowed Codex row disappears from the list, or it is shown with "Uncheck shown" disabled, which is the #689 bug again. All tests in `tests/admin-capacity-status.test.ts` still pass. During review, a scratch VM test that ran the real `providersVisibleEntries` and `renderProvidersPicker` with selection `["sub-a"]` and "Only active" on failed on the pre-fix base 36503598 and passed on the PR head. That shows a test can catch this. It was not committed.

**Suggested fix.** Add the real filter and re-render code to the `providerPicker` VM, then add one case for this path:

- Add `between("const providersFilterIsActive =", "/**\n * Provider health")` (it holds `providersFilterIsActive` and `providersVisibleEntries`, `static/admin.js:9829-9856`) and `between("const renderProvidersPicker =", "const applyProvidersSelection =")` to the slice list.
- Remove the `providersVisibleEntries` and `providersFilterIsActive` stubs. Add the inputs the real code reads: `providerTierFilter`, `providersSearchInput` and `providersSortSelect` (each with a `value`), plus `providersEntryMatchesQuery` and `providersDisplayOrderIds`. Either slice those from `static/admin.js:9813` and `:9695` or stub them. Stub `renderProvidersMessage` and `buildProviderEntry` and keep the DOM stubbed as it is now.
- Let the fixture take an `onlyActive` flag that sets `providersOnlyActiveInput.checked`. Keep the current tier-filter cases working, for example by setting `providerTierFilter = "subscription"` where they now pass `visibleIds: ["codex"]`.
- New test: selection `["sub-a"]`, "Only active" on, tier filter `all`. Assert that the shown ids are exactly `["codex"]` and that "Uncheck shown" is enabled with the text "Uncheck 1 shown". Click it, then assert the selection is empty, the list re-renders with no rows, and "Uncheck shown" is disabled.
- Check that the new test fails if `providersVisibleEntries` drops the `providerCodexSelection().selected > 0` clause, or if `updateProvidersStatus` goes back to counting with `providerSelection.has(id)`.

The fixture runs `admin.js` code in a VM. Keep the test in `tests/admin-capacity-status.test.ts`, because that is the only file with the `sonarjs/code-eval` exemption in `tools/lint/eslint.config.mjs`. A new file would need a change under `tools/lint/`, which is a protected path.

title: Follow-up from #1151 (issue #687): keep Codex off when its row is unchecked, block a save that leaves no tier active, fix the save toast count
body:
PR #1151 (https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/1151) fixed issue #687. It was merged in commit c47b6f87f4d28570d6b1e71b3752a4e2dc1c39a3 (https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/c47b6f87f4d28570d6b1e71b3752a4e2dc1c39a3). This issue holds the review findings from that PR that are still unresolved on development. All of them are P3, and none blocked the merge.

Since #1151, the provider picker in `static/admin.js` sends staged ids that the roster no longer lists, for example a `codex:<hash>` subscription whose account was removed. Before, it dropped them. Items 1 to 3 are cases where that new behaviour leaves the panel and the server out of step.

I checked each item against development b24353e5. The only later change to `static/admin.js` is #1152 (issue #689). It changed which bulk buttons are disabled in `updateProvidersStatus` and fixes none of these items. I ran the shipped picker functions from b24353e5 in a `node:vm` context, together with the server's `normalizeSelectedProviderIds`, `isProviderEnabled` and `codexAccountEligibility`. That run still reproduces items 1 and 2. Item 3 is plain from the code.

Line numbers are at merge commit c47b6f87. Where #1152 moved a line, the line on development b24353e5 is in brackets.

In the examples, A, B and C are configured Codex subscriptions, and R is a saved `codex:<hash>` whose account is no longer configured.

## 1. Unchecking the Codex row leaves Codex on when a missing Codex id is staged (P3)

**Where.**

- `static/admin.js:10366-10376` [10370-10380]: `setProviderChecked`. For the Codex row it deletes `codex` and the configured subscription ids only (`:10373` [10377]).
- `static/admin.js:9801-9803`: since #1151, the serializer sends every missing id that is still staged.
- `static/admin.js:10064`: the "Codex is off" warning is suppressed on purpose while any missing id is staged.
- `src/provider/selection.ts:161-166` (`isProviderEnabled`): any `codex:*` id turns Codex on. `:177-182` (`codexAccountEligibility`) narrows the account pool to the listed hashes.

**Problem.** Unchecking the Codex row does not remove a missing `codex:*` id, so the save still names one Codex subscription. On the server that keeps Codex on, with a pool narrowed to an account that does not exist. Before #1151 the same save sent nothing for Codex and turned it off.

**Failure scenario.** The configured subscriptions are A and B, and the saved selection is `[R, A, surplus]`. The operator unchecks the Codex row. The staged set becomes `{R, surplus}`, and Save sends `[surplus, R]`.

- On the server, Codex stays enabled with zero eligible accounts (`src/codex/routing-serial.ts:295-305`), and `/v1/models` keeps listing the Codex models (`src/models/catalog.ts:112`).
- The panel shows the Codex row unchecked and "1 of 3 providers active: Surplus.", plus the missing-subscription warning. Because of the suppression at `:10064`, nothing says that Codex is still on.

**Suggested fix.** When the Codex row is unchecked, also delete the staged missing `codex:*` ids, because turning the tier off covers them. Alternatively, show the Codex row as partial (indeterminate) while a missing `codex:*` id is staged, so the operator can see that Codex is still on. Add the case to the VM-based picker test in `tests/admin-capacity-status.test.ts`.

## 2. Save stays enabled for a selection that leaves no tier active (P3)

**Where.**

- `static/admin.js:10155` [10159]: Save is disabled only when the staged set is empty.
- `static/admin.js:10282` [10286]: `saveProviderSelection` has the same guard.

**Problem.** A staged set that holds only missing ids is not empty, so Save stays enabled even though no tier is checked. One click then stores a restriction that routes nothing.

**Failure scenario.** The saved selection is `[R, surplus]`. The operator presses "Uncheck all", which leaves `{R}` staged. Save is enabled. The summary reads "0 of 3 providers active." and the panel warns "Both paid tiers are off". Saving stores `[R]`: Codex is nominally on with no eligible account, and every other provider is off, so no request can route. Without a missing id, the same "Uncheck all" empties the selection and Save stays disabled. The #1151 PR description lists this under Known limitations.

**Suggested fix.** Disable Save, or ask for confirmation, when the serialized list is non-empty but no roster tier is checked: `providersSelectedIds().length > 0` and `providersRosterIds().filter(isProviderChecked)` is empty. Put the same check in `saveProviderSelection`, so a save cannot bypass the button.

## 3. The save toast counts staged ids, not active tiers (P3)

**Where.** `static/admin.js:10308` [10312]: the success toast reads `` `${formatNumber(providerSelection.size)} providers active` ``.

**Problem.** `providerSelection` holds ids, not tiers. A missing id counts as a provider, and a narrowed Codex tier counts once per subscription. The panel badge (`:10131` [10135]) and the summary count tiers, so the toast disagrees with both. #1151 added the missing-id case. The narrowed-subscription case was already there.

**Failure scenario.**

- After saving `[R]`, the toast says "1 providers active", while the summary says "0 of 3 providers active.".
- With subscriptions A, B and C configured, saving `[A, B, surplus]` reports "3 providers active" for two active tiers. The badge says "2 active".

**Suggested fix.** Count tiers the way the badge does: `providersRosterIds().filter(isProviderChecked).length`. Also make the noun singular for a count of one. #1169 also changes this save handler and asks for the toast to be counted from the saved selection, so the two fixes can land together.

## 4. The #1151 PR description has a non-standard footer (P3, no code change)

**Where.** The description of PR #1151.

**Problem.** The description ends with `---` and `_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_…)_`. The house form for PR descriptions is the line `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)`, a blank line, then the session URL. Merged #1136 uses the house form.

**Failure scenario.** Nothing at runtime. Only the description text is affected, and nothing in the code or the merge depends on it.

**Suggested fix.** Edit the merged PR's description to the house form, or close this item as not worth doing.

## Related

- #1169 (from #1150): the Providers tab drops checkbox edits made while a save is pending. It touches the same `saveProviderSelection` code as item 3.
- #1060, Sentinel's candidate PR for #687, is still open. #1151 supersedes it, and closing it is left to the owner.

title: Follow-up from #1150 (issue #669): Providers tab drops checkbox edits made while a save is pending
body:
PR #1150 (https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/1150) fixed issue #669 for the Models tab. It was merged in commit f2457327beae47f991c31038365a5cbd2deb917b (https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/f2457327beae47f991c31038365a5cbd2deb917b). This issue holds the review finding from that PR that is still unresolved on development.

The review's P2 finding was that a whitelist save which returns after `invalidateAdminModels` leaves the Models panel in a false "Unsaved changes" state. That defect is already tracked in #668, and I added the post-#1150 evidence there: https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/issues/668#issuecomment-6243849742. It is not repeated here.

## 1. The Providers tab drops checkbox edits made while a save is pending (P3)

**Where.** Line numbers are at merge commit f2457327. On development b24353e5 the same lines are 17 higher (shown in brackets).

- `static/admin.js:10263` [10280]: `saveProviderSelection`.
- `static/admin.js:10277` [10294]: the POST body is `providersSelectedIds()`, read when Save is clicked.
- `static/admin.js:10289` [10306]: `const savedIds = Array.isArray(payload?.provider_ids) ? payload.provider_ids : providersSelectedIds();`. The fallback reads the selection again after the response arrives.
- `static/admin.js:10291` [10308]: `providerSelection = new Set(providersSavedSelection);` replaces the staged selection with the saved one.
- `static/admin.js:9883` [9893] and `static/admin.js:9953` [9963]: the provider and subscription checkboxes are not disabled while a save is pending. `updateProvidersStatus` disables only the bulk buttons, Discard and Save.
- `static/admin.js:10388` [10405]: the `providersList` change listener updates `providerSelection` at any time, including while a save is pending.

**Problem.** This is the same bug #669 fixed for the Models tab. On success, the save handler overwrites the staged selection with the saved one. Any checkbox the operator changed after clicking Save is lost, and the panel looks clean, so nothing tells them. If the response has no `provider_ids`, the fallback reads the selection after the response arrived and records an edit that was never sent as saved. The current server always returns `provider_ids` (`src/admin/codex.ts`, `handleAdminProviderSelectionSet`), so the fallback only matters for an older server or a proxy that strips the field.

**Failure scenario.** The roster is `a, b, c` and the saved selection is all three, which is the no-filter state. The operator narrows the staged selection to `[a]` and clicks Save. While the POST is pending, they check `b`.

- If the response includes `provider_ids: ["a"]`, both saved and staged become `[a]` and the panel shows no unsaved changes. The `b` check is gone, and routing keeps `b` disabled although the operator just enabled it.
- If the response has no `provider_ids`, saved and staged both become `[a, b]` and the panel shows no unsaved changes. The panel now says `b` is saved and active, but the server stored only `[a]`, so routing still skips `b`.

I reproduced both cases by running the shipped `static/admin.js` from development b24353e5 in a `node:vm` context. The test used the real provider state, the selection helpers, `saveProviderSelection` and the `providersList` change listener, with only fetch and rendering faked:

```
with provider_ids:    {"requests":[{"provider_ids":["a"]}],"state":{"saved":["a"],"staged":["a"],"saving":false},"unsaved":false}
without provider_ids: {"requests":[{"provider_ids":["a"]}],"state":{"saved":["a","b"],"staged":["a","b"],"saving":false},"unsaved":false}
```

**Suggested fix.** Do what #1150 did for Models (`modelsSelectionAfterSave`, `static/admin.js:9075`):

- When Save is clicked, take a snapshot of the staged set (`const submittedSelection = new Set(providerSelection)`) and the ids to send (`const submittedIds = providersSelectedIds()`). Send exactly `submittedIds`.
- On success, set `providersSavedSelection = providersSelectionFromIds(Array.isArray(payload?.provider_ids) ? payload.provider_ids : submittedIds)`.
- Rebuild `providerSelection` from the saved set, then replay the edits made since Save was clicked. Drop every id in `submittedSelection` that is no longer in `providerSelection`, and add every id in `providerSelection` that was not in `submittedSelection`.
- Do the replay on the internal staged set, not on the serialized `provider_ids`. `providersSelectedIds()` turns "every provider checked" into `[]`, and the `codex` umbrella stands in for its subscriptions, so diffing the serialized lists would give the wrong answer.
- Count the toast from the saved selection.

Add a fixture-VM test like `tests/admin-models-save-pending.test.ts` that covers four cases: a check while the save is pending, an uncheck while the save is pending, a response with no `provider_ids`, and a Codex subscription toggled while the save is pending.

Two related issues are separate and should stay that way: #680 (a provider save response that arrives after a target change is still applied) and #679 (edits made during a roster GET are replaced). A fix here can add the same load-generation check (`providerSelectionLoadId`) that #680 asks for.
