title: Follow-up from #1160 (issue #1139): make stale-lock recovery in the signing helper race-free and resolve #1159 onto it
body:
PR #1160 (https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/1160), which fixed #1139, merged as https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/ed0ecdda85ee261bc8388558bb26c2c86f5ac9a5. Its review found no P0 or P1 issues and all four checks were green, so it merged. The review left the five findings below open: one P2 and four P3.

I checked each one against development at `b24353e5`. `ops/gpg-dsh.sh` and `tests/gpg-dsh.test.ts` have not changed since the merge, so findings 1-3 still apply as written. Finding 4 still applies too: #1159 conflicts with development in all three files. Line numbers are at the merge commit `ed0ecdda`.

The helper is the Mac-local `gpg.program` wrapper, installed by hand. Nothing in the VPS release path or in ubiquity/sentinel calls it, so none of this touches a deployed interface. Every failure seen in the review was fail-closed (exit 2). No run published a deleted key under a current manifest stamp.

## 1. P2: breaking a stale lock is check-then-delete, so waiters remove each other's fresh locks

**Where:**
- `ops/gpg-dsh.sh:156-162`: the stale-lock branch of `take_lock`.
- `ops/gpg-dsh.sh:158-159`: the owner check and the `rm -rf "$lock"` that follows it.
- `docs/DECISIONS.md:591` and `:602-603`: "Rebuilds are serialized and published whole" and the stale-lock sentence.

**Problem:** When a lock holder is killed mid-rebuild, every waiter reaches the 15-second mark at about the same time. Each one reads the owner file, sees that it is unchanged, and runs `rm -rf "$lock"`. The read and the delete are two steps, so this sequence is possible:
1. Waiter W1 and waiter W2 both read the stale owner.
2. W1 removes the lock, loops, and wins `mkdir`.
3. W2, which already passed its check, runs `rm -rf` on W1's fresh lock.

Several calls then hold "the" lock and rebuild at once. That breaks the serialization the decision entry and the PR description promise. The PR body says "a lock is only removed while its owner file is unchanged", and the recovery test (`tests/gpg-dsh.test.ts:248`) runs only one caller.

**Failure scenario:** The review's stress setup was a stale lock plus a leftover `.new.*` stage (a SIGKILLed holder), an input change, then 16 concurrent sandboxed calls. Over 60 rounds (960 calls), 15 calls exited 2 with one of these errors:
- `cannot create .../<uid>.lock/owner: Directory nonexistent`: another waiter deleted the lock between this call's `mkdir` and its owner write.
- `cannot break the stale rebuild lock ...` with `rm: ... Is a directory`: two `rm -rf` runs raced on the same tree.
- `cannot set the stale seed ... aside`: two holders were swapping at once.

In one more round, two calls exited 0 but the fake gpg saw no key, so real gpg would have failed those signings. In 7 of the 60 rounds the agent was stopped 2-3 times instead of once. For the owner, this means some sandboxed `git commit -S` calls fail after a crash or a killed signing, even though the helper says it recovers.

**Suggested fix:** Serialize the lock breakers:
1. Take a second `mkdir` lock, `$lock.break`.
2. Under it, check that the owner file is still the stale value you read.
3. Remove `$lock`, then `rmdir "$lock.break"`.

A breaker that cannot take `$lock.break` goes back to waiting. When the `rm` fails, `continue` the loop instead of calling `die`. Add a test: a stale lock plus N concurrent calls must all exit 0, with exactly one `gpgconf --kill`.

## 2. P3: a negative `held` breaks a live lock

**Where:** `ops/gpg-dsh.sh:140-141` (`now` is sampled, then the owner file is read) and `:156` (the `[ "$held" -lt 0 ]` branch).

**Problem:** `take_lock` reads the clock before it reads the owner file. Suppose the lock is released, and a new holder takes it and writes its start time in the next second, all between those two reads. Then `started` is `now + 1`, `held` is -1, and the `-lt 0` branch treats the lock as stale. The check at `:158` passes, because the owner the waiter just read is still the current one. So the waiter deletes a live lock.

**Failure scenario:** The review reproduced this deterministically by slowing the owner read so it crosses a second boundary while a second holder takes the lock. The waiter printed `breaking the stale rebuild lock ... (owner: 222 1792271135)` 0.44 s after that holder took the lock, and removed it. With a 0.5 s owner-read delay, 25 rounds of 16 calls broke 197 live locks, though with 0 failures and 0 double rebuilds. Without the delay, about 150 rounds under dash and 30 under `bash --posix` showed no lock breaks. So this is rare in practice. When it happens it allows two concurrent rebuilds, the precondition for finding 3. It can also fail the CI assertion "each input change rebuilds the seed, and stops its agent, exactly once" (`tests/gpg-dsh.test.ts:219`) at random.

**Suggested fix:** Read the owner file first, then sample `now`. Then `now >= started` for any owner written before the read. A negative `held` can then only mean clock skew, so treat it as live (or re-sample) instead of stale.

## 3. P3: the "reappeared" guard and the final `mv` are check-then-act

**Where:** `ops/gpg-dsh.sh:211-214`, in `rebuild_seed`.

**Problem:** The guard checks that `$seed` does not exist and then runs `mv "$stage" "$seed"`. If two calls hold the lock at once (through finding 1 or 2), both can pass the guard. The first `mv` renames its stage to `$seed`. The second `mv` then moves its stage into the published seed, as `$seed/<uid>.new.XXXXXX`. `has_leftovers` and `discard_leftovers` (`:174-187`) only look at siblings of `$seed`, so nothing removes it.

**Failure scenario:** This is theoretical: it did not show up in the 60 killed-holder rounds. Holders A and B both pass the guard. A publishes its stage. B's stage, holding copies of the private keys, lands inside A's seed, and B signs from A's seed. If a key was deleted between B's manifest read and A's, B's nested copy of that deleted key stays on disk inside the current seed until the next input change. gpg does not read it, but the copy persists, which is the outcome #587 and #1139 set out to prevent.

**Suggested fix:** Fixing findings 1 and 2 removes the precondition. As a backstop, after the swap, check that `$seed` contains no `*.new.*` or `*.old.*` entries, and fail closed (removing them) if it does. Alternatively, use `mv -T` where it exists. It is GNU-only, so feature-detect it: the owner's Mac uses BSD `mv`.

## 4. P3: open PR #1159 (#1141) conflicts with development in all three helper files

**Where:** `docs/DECISIONS.md`, `ops/gpg-dsh.sh` (the rebuild section, from `:197`) and `tests/gpg-dsh.test.ts`.

**Problem:** #1159 rewrites the same part of `ops/gpg-dsh.sh` as #1160: a per-uid `dsh-gnupg-<uid>/seed` layout, one hashing process, and refusing planted seed config files. #1160 merged first, so #1159 now has to be resolved by hand. #1160's Known limitations section names the moves needed:
- The lock and sibling names come from `$seed` (`$seed.lock`, `$seed.new.*`, `$seed.old.*`), so they work unchanged with the new layout.
- #1159's planted-config check belongs in `read_recorded`.
- #1159's `copy_inputs` must write into `$stage`, not `$seed`.

**Failure scenario:** `git merge-tree` of #1159's head `2892d609` against development `b24353e5` reports content conflicts in all three files. A resolution that keeps #1159's in-place copy brings back the writes into a published seed that #1160 removed. A resolution that keeps #1160's `read_recorded` unchanged drops #1159's refusal of planted `gpg-agent.conf`/`gpg.conf` files (the pinentry-capture issue in #1141). In either case CI could stay green, because each PR's tests cover only its own half.

**Suggested fix:** Resolve #1159 onto development by hand as described above. Then re-run `tests/gpg-dsh.test.ts` and a concurrency stress (stale lock plus N concurrent calls) on the combined helper before #1159 is re-reviewed. If findings 1-3 are fixed first, fold them into the same resolution.

## 5. P3: the PR description ending does not match house style (no repository change)

**Where:** the description of #1160.

**Problem:** It ends with the session URL followed by `---` and `_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_`, which the PR tooling appended. Merged #1123, #1124 and #1136 instead end with "Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)", a blank line, then the session URL. Patching the body through MCP and through the REST API produced the same rewrite.

**Failure scenario:** None for the code. The record differs from the rest of the series, as already noted for #1134 and #1137 in #1141.

**Suggested fix:** If the record should match, the owner can edit the description. No commit is needed.

## Not a finding: the owner's install step from #1139 is still open

`Resolves #1139` closed the issue at merge, but item 2's machine step was never something the PR could do. Merging installs nothing on the Mac. If it is not already done, run `diff ops/gpg-dsh.sh ~/bin/gpg-dsh`, check that the installed helper does not seed `gpg.conf`, `gpg-agent.conf` or `public-keys.d`, and then run `install -m 0755 ops/gpg-dsh.sh ~/bin/gpg-dsh`. If you do that before findings 1-3 are fixed, the helper's only weak spot is recovery after a killed or hung signing. The common case, a burst of commits after one key change, is fixed.

title: Follow-up from #1158 (issue #1131): keep the owner-index wait off VPS failure responses and pace the fill
body:
PR #1158 (https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/1158), which fixed #1131, merged as https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/27fcf4ed99d020b15711d613d127266c691f001d. Its review found no P0 or P1 issues and all four checks were green on the reviewed head `24fae239`, so it merged. The review left the four non-blocking findings below open.

I checked each one against development at `2c7f1378`. None of the files involved have changed since the merge, so all four still apply. Line numbers are at the merge commit `27fcf4ed` and are the same on `2c7f1378`.

#1158 changes no interface that ubiquity/sentinel uses. Its diff is limited to the three `src/sentinel/replay-retention*.ts` files and one test, and the sentinel repository references none of them.

## 1. P2: on the VPS, the 500 ms owner-index wait sits in front of client-visible failure responses

**Where:**
- `src/sentinel/replay-retention-bootstrap.ts:354`: `prepareChunkOwners` waits for the fill for up to `BOOTSTRAP_OWNER_INDEX_WAIT_MS`.
- `src/sentinel/replay-retention-schema.ts:52`: `BOOTSTRAP_OWNER_INDEX_WAIT_MS = 500`.
- `src/handler/http.ts:22-41`: `scheduleSentinelBackgroundTask` defers work only when `globalThis.EdgeRuntime.waitUntil` exists.
- Where the replay task is awaited inline when it does not exist: `src/handler/terminal-log.ts:478` (non-SSE failure response), `src/handler/terminal-route.ts:170` (propagated gateway exception), `src/handler/terminal-route.ts:268-271` (pre-capture rejection) and `src/handler/terminal-route.ts:465-468` (thrown inference failure with no captured body).
- The two waits a failed request can hit: `src/sentinel/replay-retention.ts:872` (`reserveSentinelReplayCapacity` calls `runBootstrapBatch`) and `src/sentinel/replay-retention.ts:110` (`admitSentinelReplayStatusMetadata` calls `bootstrapBeforeMutation`).

**Problem:** The Known limitations section of #1158 says the callers that wait are "capture and status tasks that run after the response", and that a request waits "once per process and sweep". Neither holds on the VPS. Nothing in the Bun VPS process defines `EdgeRuntime.waitUntil`, and no caller passes a `waitUntil`. So `scheduleSentinelBackgroundTask` returns false, and each call site above awaits the replay task before it returns the response or rethrows the error. Also, every batch that arrives while a fill is running waits, not only the first one.

**Failure scenario:**
1. The store's sweep is at its chunk phase. #1131 notes production may be stuck at `1|`.
2. The process restarts. Filling the index then takes about 0.6-3 s (20,000-100,000 owner rows at about 30,000 rows/s).
3. In that window, a failed request can wait twice: up to 500 ms in the refused reservation, then up to another 500 ms in the refused capture's status write. Before #1158 each of these calls read one 64-row slice, which took a few ms.

A review probe with a slowed fill measured 501-506 ms per status admission and about 910 ms for a refused reservation. About 500 ms of the 910 ms is the bootstrap wait; the rest comes from how the probe slowed reads. The extra latency is bounded and transient, and it affects failure responses only.

**Suggested fix:**
- Give the inference-path callers (`reserveSentinelReplayCapacity` and the status-metadata admission) a zero or very small wait, and keep the bounded wait for maintenance and admin views only. A batch that does not wait leaves the sweep where it is, which it already does when the wait times out.
- Or, on those paths, start the fill without waiting for it.
- Correct the doc wording so that the owner decides the 500 ms value (an open owner question on #1158) knowing that on the VPS it sits in front of failure responses.

## 2. P3: the background fill runs unpaced, and keeps reading after another process finishes the sweep

**Where:** `src/sentinel/replay-retention-bootstrap.ts:300-303` (`fillChunkOwnerIndex`), which loops over `advanceChunkOwnerIndex` (`:276-297`).

**Problem:** The fill reads one 64-row slice after another with no pause between them. It stops only when it completes or when this handle no longer holds the index. If another process finishes the sweep, this handle's fill keeps reading until it completes, or until a later `bootstrapBeforeMutation` or `reserveSentinelReplayCapacity` call on this handle sees the complete ledger and drops the index.

**Failure scenario:** With 100,000 owner rows, the fill makes about 1,600 back-to-back 64-row list calls in about 3 s, validating each row on the main thread while the process serves traffic. If a second process completes the sweep in the meantime, the first process still runs the full scan. The cost is wasted reads and CPU, bounded by one full owner scan. Correctness is not affected.

**Suggested fix:** Yield or pace between slices. Stop the fill early when a cheap ledger read shows the sweep is complete or carries a different `bootstrap_sweep` id.

## 3. P3: after a ledger-only restore, the retired stand-in stalls the restored sweep until restart

**Where:** `src/sentinel/replay-retention-bootstrap.ts:469` (`settleChunkOwnerIndex` installs the retired stand-in), `:354-356` (a retired index is never waited on and never ready), and the restore note at `:238-240`.

**Problem:** Once a commit on a handle moves sweep S past its chunk phase, the handle holds a retired stand-in for S that never fills. If an older copy of the ledger alone is then restored, with S back at a chunk cursor, that handle can never judge S's chunks again.

**Failure scenario:**
1. On process A, sweep S passes its chunk phase, so A holds `emptyChunkOwnerIndex(S, true)`.
2. Someone restores only an older ledger copy, with S at a chunk cursor.
3. Every batch on A finds the retired stand-in, judges no chunk, and returns the ledger unchanged. Admissions on A stay refused until A restarts.

The existing note already says to restart every process after such a restore, for safety, and that instruction also covers this case. It does not say that skipping the restart also stops progress.

**Suggested fix:** Mention the liveness effect next to the restore note, or in the ops/runbook text for ledger restores.

## 4. P3: no test has a process die before its owner-index fill finishes

**Where:** `tests/sentinel-replay-bootstrap-retry.test.ts:705-732` ("a process that restarts every few calls still finishes the sweep").

**Problem:** The test seeds 200 legacy manifests, which is 4 slices. The fill reads them in a few ms, so every fresh handle completes its index during its first call. The test therefore cannot catch a regression that only shows when a process lives for less than one full fill, which is the production concern at 20,000-100,000 owner rows. The test at `:733` ("the owner index fills without further requests") covers background progress on a single handle only.

**Failure scenario:** A change that, for example, left a new handle waiting on, or sharing state with, a fill that an earlier handle never finished would still pass this test, because in it no handle ever leaves a fill unfinished. In production, at 20,000-100,000 owner rows, a restart during the 0.6-3 s fill is exactly that case.

**Suggested fix:** Add a variant that holds the fill with `holdNextList` (`:194`) across a handle swap, then assert that the next handle's fill completes and the sweep advances.

title: Follow-up from #1157 (issue #1133): fix a quota-test clock race and close gaps in the spec-pin and contract tests
body:
PR #1157 (https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/1157), which fixed #1133, merged as https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/efc3d90dd2a08e371aa709908f555ea386e6f1bb. Its review found no P0 or P1 issues and CI was green, so it merged. The review left the four P3 findings below open.

I checked each one against development at `2c7f1378`. None of the files involved have changed since the merge, so all four still apply. Line numbers are at the merge commit `efc3d90d`. While checking, I corrected two of the review's descriptions; both corrections are noted below.

## 1. P3: a clock race makes a Claude Code quota test fail at random

**Where:**
- `tests/claude-code-accounts.test.ts:486-495`: the test "quota proof is exact-model and expires at its recorded reset boundary".
- `src/provider/claude-code-quota.ts:524`: `recordClaudeCodeQuotaOutcome` reads its own clock when no `nowMs` is passed.
- `src/provider/claude-code-quota.ts:486` and `:479`: that reading becomes the proof's `observed_at_ms`.
- `src/provider/claude-code-quota.ts:150`: a proof only counts when `observed_at_ms <= nowMs`.

**Problem:** The test reads `const now = Date.now()` at line 486, then records a 429 outcome without passing `nowMs`. `recordClaudeCodeQuotaOutcome` takes its own `Date.now()` at line 524 and stores it as the proof's `observed_at_ms`. The assertion at line 495 then asks for the proof at the earlier `now`. If the millisecond clock ticks between the two readings, `observed_at_ms` is `now + 1`, the check at line 150 fails, and `claudeCodePoolProofForModel` returns null.

Correction: the review blamed the default argument of `observation()`. That value is not what the proof stores. The clock that matters is the one inside `recordClaudeCodeQuotaOutcome`, so passing `now` to `observation()` alone would not fix it.

**Failure scenario:** It has already failed twice in CI, both times on PRs that touch neither file:
- #1157, run 39063762168, attempt 1: validate failed with `AssertionError: null == true` at line 495. A rerun of the job passed.
- #1162, validate job 117507578190 in run 39070721689: the same test failed the same way. The merge step stops on any red check, so #1162 was not merged.

Any PR can hit this, and each hit blocks a merge until someone reruns the job.

**Suggested fix:** Pass the captured clock in. Add `nowMs: now` to that `recordClaudeCodeQuotaOutcome` call, and use `observation("1", now)` so both readings agree. Then check the other tests in the file for the same pattern: a proof recorded with the internal clock and read back at an earlier `Date.now()`. The next test, at line 503, already passes `response_observed_at_ms: now` and reads the proof at a later clock, so it is safe.

## 2. P3: the nullable-field contract test only covers the default Codex route

**Where:**
- `tests/openapi-nullable-request-contract.test.ts:41-52`: both request builders use `DEFAULT_TEST_MODEL`.
- `tests/openapi-nullable-request-contract.test.ts:65` and `:76`: the Chat and Responses sweeps.

**Problem:** The test sends null for each published nullable field, 20 on Chat and 18 on Responses, but only to `DEFAULT_TEST_MODEL`, which runs on the Codex route. These routes are never sent a null:
- Cerebras (`src/provider/cerebras-handlers.ts`)
- Lithos (`src/provider/lithos-handlers.ts`)
- DeepSeek (`src/deepseek/handlers.ts`)
- OpenRouter (`src/provider/openrouter-handlers.ts`)

#1157 lists this under Known limitations.

**Failure scenario:** A later change adds a strict parser to one provider, for example a `temperature` check in `cerebras-handlers.ts` that rejects null. A client sends `temperature: null` to a Cerebras model, as `/openapi.json` allows, and gets a 400. The contract test still passes, because it never sends to that route.

**Suggested fix:** Run the same sweep once per provider route. Use each provider's test model and the existing harness mocks for its upstream.

## 3. P3: `--verify-source` may accept a commit that only exists in a fork

**Where:**
- `scripts/check-openai-spec-drift.ts:52`: `pinnedSpecSource` builds the fetch URL.
- `scripts/check-openai-spec-drift.ts:124-128`: the digest check.
- `scripts/check-openai-spec-drift.ts:250-266`: `--repin`.

**Problem:** `--verify-source` fetches `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/openai-openapi/<commit>/openapi.yaml` and checks that the bytes match the pinned sha256. That proves the bytes belong to the pinned commit. It probably does not prove that the commit is in openai/openai-openapi's own history. GitHub serves commits from any fork in the same fork network under the parent repository's path. `--repin` uses the same URL, so it would record such a commit without complaint. I have not reproduced this here; it rests on how GitHub serves fork-network commits.

**Failure scenario:**
1. Someone runs `spec:drift --repin <sha>` with a commit pushed to a fork of openai/openai-openapi, and commits the new pin.
2. In CI, `--verify-source` fetches that commit through the parent URL, the digest matches, and the gate passes.
3. The pin now names a commit OpenAI never published.

The change still needs a reviewed edit to `scripts/openai-spec-pin.json`, so the risk is low.

**Suggested fix:** In `--repin`, and optionally in `--verify-source`, confirm that the official default branch contains the commit. For example, the GitHub compare API from the pinned commit to the default branch should report `ahead` or `identical`, never `diverged`. Alternatively, make review of every pin change an explicit rule.

## 4. P3: the `/uos/` route-parity scan misses paths built from a prefix, and has no allowlist

**Where:**
- `tests/openapi-runtime-contract.test.ts:131-137`: the three dispatch patterns.
- `tests/openapi-runtime-contract.test.ts:176-188`: the scan for `/uos/` string literals.

**Problem:** The parity test finds routes in two ways. It matches three fixed `req.method === "..." && path === "..."` shapes, and it treats every `"/uos/..."` string literal under `src/` as a route that must be published.
- A path built from a prefix that has no trailing slash is seen by neither, for example `` `${UOS}/probe` `` with `const UOS = "/uos"`, or a path joined from segments.
- A real non-route literal, such as a doc link `"/uos/probe"`, fails the test, and there is no allowlist to add it to.

Correction: the review said template and concatenated paths are missed. I ran the scan's regex on sample sources. It does catch `` `/uos/${name}` `` and `"/uos/" + name`: both are reported as unpublished, so the test fails rather than staying silent. A log message that contains spaces, such as `"/uos/probe is deprecated"`, is not matched. The gap is the prefix and joined forms above.

**Failure scenario:** A new module defines `const UOS = "/uos"` and dispatches `` path === `${UOS}/probe` ``. The route ships unpublished, and both parity tests pass. Separately, a later change adds a doc link `"/uos/probe"` to an error message. The test fails, and the only way to pass it is to publish the path or reword the message.

**Suggested fix:** Longer term, export the UOS route table from the router and compare the published paths against it, as #1133 suggested. When the first real non-route literal appears, add an explicit allowlist constant to the test.

title: Follow-up from #1155 (issue #1125): bound pending VPS join windows and their checkpoint growth
body:
PR #1155 (https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/1155) fixed #1125 and was merged as [`2de00a80f812901680bd6e1109e90fbc7f0dac24`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/2de00a80f812901680bd6e1109e90fbc7f0dac24). Its review found no P0 or P1 problem, so it merged. The review left one P2 and two P3 findings, which are filed here as follow-up work. Line references are to the merge commit. The files involved have not changed on `development` since (tip `2c7f1378`), and I re-checked each finding against that code.

Nothing in `src/` or `serve.ts` imports these modules, and `sentinel-release` is disabled, so none of this affects production today. It starts to matter once Sentinel's VPS release bridge is re-pinned to a driver that includes #1027 (ubiquity/sentinel#150).

## 1. P2: a request lost to a crash keeps its window collecting until the deadline

**Where:**
- [`ops/vps-release-metrics.ts:71`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/2de00a80f812901680bd6e1109e90fbc7f0dac24/ops/vps-release-metrics.ts#L71) skips PID 1 rows.
- [`ops/vps-release-metrics.ts:318-331`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/2de00a80f812901680bd6e1109e90fbc7f0dac24/ops/vps-release-metrics.ts#L318-L331) is the `_scan` loop.
- [`ops/vps-release-metrics.ts:351`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/2de00a80f812901680bd6e1109e90fbc7f0dac24/ops/vps-release-metrics.ts#L351) reports `deadline_exceeded`.
- [`ops/vps-metrics-join.ts:93`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/2de00a80f812901680bd6e1109e90fbc7f0dac24/ops/vps-metrics-join.ts#L93) keeps the slices.

**Problem:** #1125 asked for PID 1 rows about the unit to be skipped, and `checkedRow` now skips them. Before #1155, such a row refused its slice. Examples are systemd's "Main process exited" or "Started ..." rows after a crash. That refusal was the only thing that ended a window whose request never logged a terminal, and nothing replaced it. A window that has an admission but no terminal stays `pending`, so `_scan` keeps reading forward, up to 16 reads per tick, until the operation deadline. All that time, `pruneJoinLedgers` keeps every slice from the window's `scanStart`, so the checkpoint keeps growing.

**Failure scenario:** during monitoring, the candidate crashes, is OOM-killed or gets SIGKILL while requests are in flight, so those requests never log a terminal. The reviewer simulated this at 0.35 req/s, with 1 in 10 requests a 5-minute stream and a crash at window 10:
- The #1027 code refused window 0 at tick 11 (`coverage_missing`), and monitoring restarted.
- The merged code keeps window 0 at `collecting`/`terminal_or_slice_pending` through tick 120. The checkpoint grows linearly: 500,469 bytes at tick 80, 610,697 at tick 100 and 720,964 at tick 120.
- The window then reports `deadline_exceeded`, and the release fails at the deadline.

That outcome is safe, but a candidate that crashed once and has been healthy since now fails at the deadline instead of restarting monitoring.

**Suggested fix:** add a forward bound for pending admissions. Once the scan passes it, the window becomes unavailable, for example with a new reason `terminal_lost`. The bound can be either of these:
- a PID 1 exit or restart row for the unit after the admission. The row stays skipped as a request row but is kept as a lifecycle marker;
- or a maximum request lifetime after the admission.

Add a test with an admission, a PID 1 restart row and no terminal.

## 2. P3: an orphan terminal well after a window still refuses that window

**Where:** [`ops/vps-release-metrics.ts:181-184`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/2de00a80f812901680bd6e1109e90fbc7f0dac24/ops/vps-release-metrics.ts#L181-L184) in `joined`, used at [`:328-329`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/2de00a80f812901680bd6e1109e90fbc7f0dac24/ops/vps-release-metrics.ts#L328-L329).

**Problem:** any terminal at or after `windowStart` that has no matching admission sets `orphanFloor`. This happens even when the terminal's own lifetime shows its admission came after `windowEnd`. So a pending window whose forward scan reaches such an orphan is refused. The #1027 code did the same, and #1155 left it in place.

**Failure scenario:** there is one orphan at window 10, either an accepted-stage or a null-stage one (for example a lost admission), and windows 0 to 9 are still pending on 5-minute streams. Window 0's forward scan reaches the orphan. `orphanFloor` comes to about window 0's start plus 270 s, and `scanStart <= orphanFloor`, so window 0 is refused at tick 10. Yet the orphan's admission cannot be in window 0. The #1027 code refused the same window at tick 17, after 1,040 reads. The merged code takes 81 reads. In both cases the controller restarts monitoring, so the result is the same, it just comes earlier.

**Suggested fix (owner decision):** ignore an orphan when `at - latencyMs - VPS_METRICS_SLICE_MS >= cohort.windowEnd`. This would trust `latency_ms` in the fail-open direction, which #1155 deliberately avoids: an under-reported latency would then hide a lost admission from the window. So this is a trade-off, not a plain bug. If the owner keeps the current behaviour, record that in `docs/DECISIONS.md`.

## 3. P3: checkpoint size still grows with request rate times the longest in-flight request

**Where:**
- [`ops/vps-metrics-join.ts:89-97`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/2de00a80f812901680bd6e1109e90fbc7f0dac24/ops/vps-metrics-join.ts#L89-L97) (`pruneJoinLedgers`)
- [`ops/vps-release-metrics.ts:403`](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/2de00a80f812901680bd6e1109e90fbc7f0dac24/ops/vps-release-metrics.ts#L403) (`retainFrom`)

**Problem:** an incomplete window keeps every ledger slice from its `scanStart`, with every event in those slices, until its last terminal arrives. So the checkpoint size is not bounded by a constant. It is bounded by the request rate times the longest in-flight request. The "Known limitations" section of #1155 does not state this bound, and neither does any doc on `development`.

**Failure scenario:** the reviewer simulated a 4 MiB cap and 7-day retention:
- At 2 req/s, with 1 in 20 requests a 30-minute stream, the checkpoint reaches the cap and candidate window 18 is refused. The peak is 4,179,775 bytes.
- At 1.5 req/s, the same mix peaks at 4,128,015 bytes, which is 98% of the cap.
- At 3 req/s, with 5-minute streams plus a single 30-minute stream, it peaks at 3,528,359 bytes.

At today's production rate of about 0.35 req/s, the checkpoint stays near 1 MB, even with 1 in 10 requests a 30-minute stream.

**Suggested fix:** document the bound next to `pruneJoinLedgers` and in the release docs, with the evidence cap it implies for a given request rate and longest stream. If it matters later, shrink a pending window to its own admissions plus the terminals at or after `windowStart`, instead of keeping whole slices.

Items 1 and 3 add up: a window held open by item 1 keeps its slices for the whole time, which is the growth item 3 describes.

title: Follow-up from #1153 (issue #1126): bound stored Mac capacity rows and make the push recover from refused or slow batches
body:
PR #1153 (https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/1153), which fixed #1126, merged as https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/commit/70eade5c11f11dd565d22a6b27cf75ec8cc8c140. Its review found no P0 or P1 issues and CI was green, so it merged. The review left the three non-blocking findings below open.

I checked each one against development at `2c7f1378`. None of the files involved have changed since the merge, so all three still apply. Line numbers are at the merge commit `70eade5c`.

## 1. P2: the VPS keeps every intermediate Mac sample, about 30 rows per bucket instead of 1

**Where:**
- `src/provider/capacity-analytics.ts:41-46`: the remote row key.
- `src/provider/capacity.ts:621-624`: the Mac overwrites its bucket point.
- `src/admin/chart-source-proxy.ts:123-134`: the pending samples.
- `src/provider/capacity-analytics.ts:109-125` and `src/provider/capacity.ts:830`: the full scan on every read.

**Problem:** #1153 added `sampled_at_ms` to the remote row key, `(host, bucket_start_at_ms, sampled_at_ms)`, so that same-bucket transition points survive. The Mac keeps one point per 15-minute bucket and overwrites it on every refresh with a new `sampled_at_ms`. Each new value is newer than the acknowledged watermark, so the Mac pushes it again and the VPS stores it under a new key. The VPS therefore holds every intermediate sample instead of one point per bucket plus real transitions. `readRemoteCapacityObservations` then lists and parses all of these rows on every VPS `/admin/providers/capacity` read.

**Failure scenario:** An open Mac Analytics tab polls every 30 s. `PROVIDER_CAPACITY_READ_FRESH_MS` is `30_000`, so almost every poll refreshes and rewrites the bucket point.
- **Review probe:** it ran 240 polls (2 hours) through the real `proxyAdminChartSource` and `handleCapacityObservationIngest`. At the end the Mac held 8 points and the VPS held 240 rows (317 KB). A gap bucket on the VPS chart could draw up to 30 points where the Mac draws 1.
- **Over a week:** with the tab open, that is about 20,160 rows (about 27 MB) per host. The old `(host, bucket)` key stored at most 672.
- **Read cost:** scanning, parsing and merging 20,160 rows took 75 ms and about 23 MB of short-lived heap against an in-memory KV. Real KV decoding costs more. This runs on every 30 s VPS admin poll and every Mac proxied read, on the production KV.

The 7-day TTL puts a ceiling on it, and routing and chart correctness are not affected.

**Suggested fix:** pick one of these.
- (a) On the Mac, push only closed buckets (`bucket_start + 15 min <= snapshot time`) plus the points saved under transition keys. Each bucket then sends one row plus its transitions.
- (b) On the VPS, store the latest sample per `(host, bucket)` under a fixed key. Only true transition points get keys that include `sampled_at_ms`, and the Mac marks which points those are.
- (c) At ingest, delete older non-transition rows for the same `(host, bucket)`.

Also consider a per-host cap on stored rows, and document how long rows are kept.

## 2. P3: one bad row makes the Mac skip its whole batch for good

**Where:**
- `src/admin/chart-source-proxy.ts:160-163` and `:186`
- `src/admin/capacity-observation-sync.ts:67-68`
- `src/provider/capacity-analytics.ts:61-66`

**Problem:** The VPS rejects the whole batch with 400 if any one row is malformed, unaligned, outside its bucket, or over 16 KiB. The Mac treats 400 and 413 as `refused` and moves its watermark past the newest sample in the batch. One bad row therefore drops up to 511 valid samples sent with it. The watermark lives only in the process, so after a restart the same batch is sent, refused and skipped again.

**Failure scenario:**
1. After a restart, the Mac sends its oldest 512 samples.
2. One row is over `MAX_REMOTE_CAPACITY_OBSERVATION_BYTES`, or fails `readStoredHistoryPoint` on a VPS running a different version.
3. The VPS answers 400, and `acknowledgedSampledAtMs` jumps to the newest sample in the batch.
4. The other 511 valid rows are never pushed.

**Suggested fix:** On `refused`, retry with smaller batches, halving down to the bad row, or drop only that row. Another option is for the VPS to skip invalid rows and return a result per row instead of rejecting the whole envelope.

## 3. P3: a push that times out resends the same large batch forever

**Where:** `src/admin/chart-source-proxy.ts:19`, `:134`, `:158`, `:166-167` and `:186`

**Problem:** The push has a fixed 5 s timeout, and a timeout counts as `retry`. The watermark stays where it is, so the next poll resends the same batch of up to 512 rows (about 0.7 MB) unchanged.

**Failure scenario:** The Mac restarts with a full week of history and either of these is true:
- its uplink is slower than about 1.2 Mbit/s, or
- the VPS takes more than 5 s to commit 8 atomic batches of 64.

Every poll then times out, and the same 0.7 MB is sent again every 30 s. The watermark never moves. This brings back, on a smaller scale, the upload amplification that #1126 item 2 fixed.

**Suggested fix:** Halve the batch after each timeout, down to a floor. Alternatively, start catch-up with a smaller batch, or scale the timeout with the batch size.

## Not included

The review also raised a P3 about the footer of the #1153 PR description. I left it out because it concerns the merged PR's text, not code. Its stated reason, that the footer differs from #1134, also does not hold: #1134 ends with the same footer.

title: Make the VPS release driver loadable by a Deno host (Bun-only deploy lock and command runner)
body:
**Problem.** Sentinel's VPS release bridge loads `ops/vps-release-driver.ts` and `ops/vps-release-metrics.ts` from an owner-pinned, hash-verified driver tree, and it runs under Deno. Since the Bun migration (between `21e4a2a9` and `e50c298b`), the driver can't be loaded by a Deno host:

- `ops/vps-release-driver.ts:26` imports `ops/vps-release-journal.ts`, which imports `ops/deploy-lock.ts:2` (`import { dlopen, FFIType } from "bun:ffi"`).
- `ops/io.ts:26` (`command`, imported by the driver at :1) runs commands through `Bun.spawn`.

Loading the `e50c298b` driver in Deno fails with `Unsupported scheme "bun"`. The `e50c298b` metrics module loads on its own; it's the driver's import graph that breaks.

**Impact.** There's no runtime impact today, because sentinel-release is disabled and the bridge's pinned driver is `21e4a2a9`. But the driver can't be re-pinned to any revision at or after `e50c298b`. Sentinel's bridge update for the #1027 `VpsJournalMetrics` interface (ubiquity/sentinel#150; the generation-81 fix is ready) refuses such a pin before it evaluates any module: "trusted VPS driver needs a host that can load Bun-only modules". VPS releases through Sentinel stay blocked until the driver tree is Deno-loadable, or the bridge host runs under Bun.

**Acceptance.** One of the following:
- The driver's import graph is free of `bun:` modules and `Bun.*` globals on the paths the bridge uses: the deploy lock, the journal, and the command runner. For example, an injected lock and runner with Bun and Deno implementations, or a runtime check that picks the right one.
- Or a recorded decision that the bridge host moves to Bun, with the Sentinel side tracked in ubiquity/sentinel#150.

Either way, keep the deploy lock's exclusion semantics identical on the VPS.

**Evidence.** `git grep` on `development` (`36503598`) finds `ops/deploy-lock.ts:2` `bun:ffi` and `ops/io.ts:26` `Bun.spawn`. The driver imports both, directly or through the journal.

title: Follow-ups: minor items from the 2026-10-17 protected-path merges
body:
<!-- sentinel-followup:batch-2026-10-17 -->

This issue collects the remaining minor (P3) findings from adversarial review of the four protected-path PRs merged on 2026-10-17. None of them blocked a merge. They are grouped by PR, and each item gives the file and line on current `development` (`b4790532`), the problem and the fix. Where two reviewers reported the same thing, it appears once. None of the items below is fixed on `development`. The P2 findings have their own issues: #1135 → #1140, and #1136 → #1139 (which also carries #1136's owner install step and the decision-entry wording about it).

## #1134 (`deba31ae`): qualify terminal-truthfulness deployment acceptance (#608)

1. **The 2026-09-22 deployment entry has the same acceptance gap.**
   - Where: `docs/DECISIONS.md:1450-1476` ("Buffered-terminal fix deployed to both surfaces").
   - Problem: the entry records acceptance of `3661bcfd13` without either observation that `AGENTS.md:65-66` requires: a direct Mac-to-VPS authenticated inference request, and `/health` returning the full SHA and `vps-<full-git-sha>` in its body and identity headers. #1134 left it unchanged as out of scope and asked the owner whether to qualify it. Unlike the `2207a757fb` entry, this one says the deploy went through `deno task deploy:vps`. At `3661bcfd13`, `ops/deploy.ts:84-95` succeeds only after loopback `/health` returns the SHA and `vps-<sha>` in both the body and the `x-uos-*` headers. So the `/health` half was checked by construction but never recorded, and nothing supports the direct Mac-to-VPS half.
   - Fix: add a dated qualification note like the #608 note. If the owner has the observations, record them instead.
2. **"Nothing in this repository supplies the missing ones" claims more than the evidence shows.**
   - Where: `docs/DECISIONS.md:1080-1082`.
   - Problem: at `2207a757fb`, `ops/deploy.ts:84-101` exits 0 only after loopback `/health` returns the SHA and `vps-<sha>` in its body and in the `x-uos-git-sha`/`x-uos-deployment-id` headers. The identity in the table is exactly what the tool prints on success. The entry does not say `deploy:vps` was used, so the `/health` half is unrecorded, not shown to be unchecked. Only the direct Mac-to-VPS inference half is truly unsupported.
   - Fix: add one sentence saying this, and change the phrase to "no recorded observation supplies them".
3. **The public-route bullet reads as if it were the only authenticated VPS inference.**
   - Where: `docs/DECISIONS.md:1074-1075`.
   - Problem: the truncation reproduction and the three normal completions (`:1063-1066`) were also authenticated inference requests "on both hosts". Their path is not recorded either.
   - Fix: reword it along the lines of "None of the requests above is recorded as a direct Mac-to-VPS request; the one whose route is stated went through the public `https://ai.ubq.fi` route."
4. **The follow-up names clauses that the trigger does not have.**
   - Where: `docs/DECISIONS.md:1118-1120`.
   - Problem: the text says the G3 bullet "keeps every clause of the deployed trigger: the reasoning-only and empty-output clauses …". The trigger (`:1100`) is "no tool call, no non-empty assistant text and no refusal". The G3 bullet (`:1099-1107`) discusses the reasoning-only case and the no-tool-call clause. It has no separate empty-output clause and never discusses the refusal clause. "Reasoning-only" is a case, not a clause.
   - Fix: name the three clauses as the trigger states them and give the basis for the refusal clause, or drop "every clause".
5. **"The changelog wording" cannot be found.**
   - Where: `docs/DECISIONS.md:1086-1087`, `:1123`.
   - Problem: the follow-up now tells readers to revise "the changelog wording that calls it a 'no tool call' guard". The repository has no changelog, and this entry is the only place the phrase appears. The ambiguity predates #1134, which turned "worth revisiting" into an instruction.
   - Fix: cite the PR, release note or other place that holds that wording, or drop the instruction.

## #1135 (`3119b54d`): make a failed first VPS deployment resumable by the same SHA (#764)

1. **A crash while restoring a first deployment leaves a receipt that every retry refuses.**
   - Where: `ops/deploy.ts:289-291`. The refusal is at `:233`.
   - Problem: `restoreFirstDeployment` removes the selector (`:289`) before it saves `rolled_back` (`:290-291`). If the process is killed between the two, or `saveRecovery` fails (for example with ENOSPC), the receipt still says `prepared` or `selected` and there is no selector. The next same-SHA run then stops at "Unselected recovery candidate has no proven rollback disposition". This fails closed, but recovery needs the receipt removed by hand. The PR's Known limitations list only the window between `prepared` and the select.
   - Fix: document this window next to that one. Alternatively, save the `rolled_back` intent before removing the selector, or treat "no previous release, no selector, phase `prepared` or `selected`" as safe to restart, since nothing ran from an unselected candidate.
2. **A first-deployment retry treats every selected candidate as already restarted.**
   - Where: `ops/deploy.ts:338`, `:284-288`.
   - Problem: `restartAttempted` is set from `candidateSelected`, even when no run ever restarted the candidate. Suppose the first run crashed after saving `selected` and before `daemon-reload`, and the retry's `daemon-reload` is refused. `restoreFirstDeployment(true)` then keeps the selector, so the next unit start (for example after a reboot) runs a candidate that was never started or accepted.
   - Fix (optional): record in the receipt whether a restart was ever issued (a `restart_attempted` flag, or a phase saved just before the restart), and clear the selector when none was.
3. **`startCandidate` overwrites the `ingress_applied` phase.**
   - Where: `ops/deploy.ts:262-273`, called at `:340`.
   - Problem: on a first-deployment retry from `ingress_applied` with an unready candidate, `startCandidate` saves `prepared`, then `selected`, then `candidate_ready`. If the restart fails, the receipt no longer records that the Caddy configuration was already applied. This is harmless today, but any later logic that relies on the phase would misread the ingress state.
   - Fix: keep `ingress_applied` when `startCandidate` runs from that phase, or record the ingress state in a separate receipt field.
4. **The README's restoration sentence is too broad.**
   - Where: `ops/README.md:49-50`.
   - Problem: "A failure before Caddy applies the new configuration restores the previous release" is not always true. After a restart, `ops/deploy.ts:297-298` refuses the cross-codec rollback to a Deno-era predecessor and leaves the candidate selected. A failed restoration of the previous listener (`:304`) leaves the selector on the previous release with an unsettled receipt.
   - Fix: qualify the sentence, for example "restores a supported Bun previous release; a Deno-era predecessor is refused and needs the codec procedure below".
5. **The retry guidance conflicts with the documented deploy steps.**
   - Where: `ops/README.md:47-48`, against the steps at `:33-37`. The refusal is at `ops/deploy.ts:368`.
   - Problem: the README says to fix the fault and "rerun the same command for the same SHA", but the documented steps fetch and fast-forward first. Any outstanding receipt refuses a different SHA with "Stale deployment recovery receipt belongs to another candidate". If the candidate itself is broken and a fix is merged, following the steps leads to that refusal, and recovery needs manual reconciliation of the receipt and selector, which is not documented.
   - Fix: say that the retry must use the same SHA (do not fetch or fast-forward first), and document how to reconcile the receipt by hand when a newer SHA has to replace a faulty candidate.

## #1136 (`d11e031d`): invalidate the sandboxed-signing seed on any key change (#587)

1. **Config files planted in the seed survive.**
   - Where: `ops/gpg-dsh.sh:65-71`, `:116-117`.
   - Problem: the manifest covers only the inputs read from the real homedir, not the seed itself, and a matching manifest reuses the seed as it is. A process inside the sandbox can write `$TMPDIR`, so it can plant `gpg-agent.conf`, `gpg.conf`, `common.conf` or `scdaemon.conf` in the seed. The planted file survives until the next input change. For example, `pinentry-program <workspace>/evil-pinentry` takes effect at the next agent start (such as after a reboot) and can capture the passphrase the owner types. The sandbox can already read the encrypted keys from `~/.gnupg`, so with the passphrase it could use the key outside the sandbox. This predates #1136.
   - Fix: on every seeded call, remove or refuse any of these files that the helper did not write. Alternatively, record the seed's own config files in the manifest and rebuild on any difference.
2. **With `TMPDIR` unset, all users share `/tmp/dsh-gnupg`.**
   - Where: `ops/gpg-dsh.sh:36`, `:43`, `:56-62`.
   - Problem: on a multi-user Linux host with `TMPDIR` unset, the first user to create `/tmp/dsh-gnupg` owns it (mode 0700). Every other user's sandboxed signing then fails closed with "… is not a directory owned by uid …". A hostile owner of that directory can also swap it for a symlink to a directory the victim owns, in the gap between the helper's second `[ -L ]` test and its `[ -O ]`/`chmod` (`:59-62`). The helper then changes the mode of, and seeds (or `rm -rf`s) inside, the victim's directory. The window is very small and the impact is limited to integrity. macOS sets a per-user `TMPDIR`, so the owner's Mac is not affected.
   - Fix: use a per-uid parent such as `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dsh-gnupg-$uid`, created with `mkdir -m 700` and verified once, or fail closed when `TMPDIR` is unset. Update the reversal-risk note at `docs/DECISIONS.md:590-591` to match.
3. **Several fail-closed and recovery rules have no tests.**
   - Where: `tests/gpg-dsh.test.ts:185` (only a symlinked seed is tested). The rules are at `ops/gpg-dsh.sh:38-41`, `:56-63` and `:102-107`.
   - Problem: no test covers a `dsh-gnupg` parent that is not a directory or is owned by another user, an existing 0755 parent or seed being tightened to 0700, a relative `TMPDIR`, or recovery from an interrupted rebuild (a seed with no `.gpg-dsh-manifest`). A regression in `private_dir` or in the missing-manifest path would pass CI.
   - Fix: add fixture cases. Pre-create `dsh-gnupg` at 0755 and assert 0700 afterwards. Replace it with a regular file and assert exit 2 with gpg never run. Set a relative `TMPDIR` and assert exit 2. Delete the manifest from a built seed and assert a rebuild plus a `gpgconf --kill`.
4. **The target platform is not tested in CI, and hashing starts one process per file.**
   - Where: `ops/gpg-dsh.sh:47-50`, `:73-80`.
   - Problem: the helper runs on the owner's Mac (bash 3.2 as `/bin/sh`, BSD `mktemp` and `cp`, `shasum`), but `tests/gpg-dsh.test.ts` runs only on Linux. Neither macOS job in `.github/workflows/deno-deploy.yml` runs it. Without `sha256sum`, every sandboxed call starts one `perl`-based `shasum` per seeded file, which adds latency to every sandboxed commit.
   - Fix: hash all inputs in one `sha256sum`/`shasum` call, or add `tests/gpg-dsh.test.ts` to a macOS CI job.

## #1137 (`b4790532`): throttle the replay metadata recount on admin polls (#785)

1. **A failed recount still repeats on every poll.**
   - Where: `src/sentinel/replay-retention-metadata.ts:92-93`, `:124-140`.
   - Problem: a recount that fails because a status or tombstone row is corrupt or mismatched records no marker. Every admin poll then repeats the strong scan up to the bad row, which can be up to 50,001 rows, and an open analytics view polls every 30 seconds. The throttle does not bound this case. The behaviour is unchanged from before and is listed under Known limitations, but it is the per-poll traversal that #785 set out to remove.
   - Fix: add a separate backoff for scan failures, for example a `failed_at` marker or a failure field on the existing marker. Set it only when `scanMetadata` returns `failed`, so a lost CAS still retries on the next poll.
2. **The marker write has no check of its own.**
   - Where: `src/sentinel/replay-retention-metadata.ts:100-103`, `:136`.
   - Problem: the marker is written with a plain `set`, and the commit checks only the ledger version. Two concurrent due polls can therefore both scan up to 50,001 rows. If they commit out of order, the marker can move back by the gap between their timestamps. Correctness is not affected; the cost is duplicated work and a slightly earlier next recount.
   - Fix (optional): pass the marker's versionstamp from the read at `:136` and add a check on it to the same atomic commit, so only one of the concurrent due polls records the recount.
3. **Stale counters can move the full recount onto the inference path.**
   - Where: `src/sentinel/replay-retention.ts:179-180`.
   - Problem: before #1137, an open dashboard recounted every 30 seconds, which kept counters left stale by TTL deletion close to the live rows. Now they can stay high for up to 15 minutes plus the KV's TTL collection delay. When they reach a bound, the next status admission or publish runs the strong recount (up to 50,001 rows) inside `pruneCaptureOwnedStatusMetadata`, on the request path. Nothing is lost (a probe confirmed `status_pruned_records` stays 0), and this already happened whenever no dashboard was open. Only the latency moves.
   - Fix (optional): let maintenance recount early, ignoring the interval, when the ledger is within some margin of `SENTINEL_REPLAY_MAX_STATUS_RECORDS` or of the metadata reserve.
4. **The doc says a poll inside the interval "writes nothing".**
   - Where: `docs/sentinel.md:322-323`.
   - Problem: only the recount writes nothing. The same maintenance pass still commits the reaper cursor and the other bounded accounting writes, as the PR's Known limitations say.
   - Fix: say that the recount reads one marker row and writes nothing, or add "for the metadata recount".

   - Where: `src/auth/index.ts:202-203`, `src/auth/local-admin.ts:22`, `src/config.ts:5`.

So `DENO_TIMELINE=production bun serve.ts --disable-admin-auth` would still let loopback clients in as admin. The real VPS entrypoint never enables this, so production is safe today. But the `isProductionTimeline` comment ("never grants development auth bypasses") claims more than the code enforces.

2. **The VPS-entrypoint test only scans the text of one file.**

## #1077 (`a7ea46b6`): give explicitly selected live e2e a destination-scoped network policy (#1041)

1. **On macOS, the live run allows all of local loopback, not one destination.**
   - Where: `README.md:22`, `scripts/test-network.ts:139-140`, `:233`.
   - Problem: the README says the live segment "admits exactly one destination". On macOS, though, the live plan ignores the port and reuses the normal macOS sandbox (Seatbelt) profile, which allows `localhost:*`. This allows no more than the normal test profile does.
   - Fix: reword the README for macOS, or add port scoping there.
2. **Live e2e on macOS still cannot reach the default `https://ai.ubq.fi`.**
   - Where: `scripts/test-network.ts:141`, `scripts/test-runner.ts:164`.
   - Problem: the run now stops safely at validation instead of failing at connect time. The PR left this as an owner decision.
   - Fix, if wanted: a scoped CONNECT relay, or something similar, for non-loopback destinations on macOS.
3. **Hostname mapping only works when name lookup reads `/etc/hosts` first.**
   - Where: `scripts/test-network.ts:215-218`.
   - Problem: some hosts look names up through a resolver daemon before reading `/etc/hosts`: `nsswitch.conf` lists `resolve` before `files` (Arch's default), or nscd is running. There the hostname resolves to the public IP, which has no route inside the test namespace. Live e2e then always fails on such hosts, though it fails safely.
   - Fix: also bind-mount a private `nsswitch.conf` with `hosts: files`, and hide `/run/nscd` and `/run/systemd/resolve` inside the live namespace.
4. **Missing system tools are found only after the native build.**
   - Where: `scripts/test-runner.ts:163-164`, `scripts/test-network.ts:235`.
   - Problem: the comment says a destination that cannot be scoped fails before the native build. But `ip` and `mount` are looked up later, in `runFile`. On a host without `mount`, the run builds native KV for minutes before it fails.
   - Fix: look up the plan's tools in `validatedGroups` as well.
5. **Other processes run by the same user can use the relay socket during a live run.**
   - Where: `scripts/test-network.ts:166`, `:179`.
   - Problem: the socket sits in a directory under `TMPDIR` that other processes can find. A concurrent ordinary test run by the same user, for example in another worktree, can reach the approved host through it. The relay only ever connects to that one origin, and the PR documents this.
   - Fix: put the socket where only the live namespace can see it, pass the listening file descriptor instead of a path, or check the connecting process with `SO_PEERCRED`.
6. **The relay directory is left behind after SIGKILL.**
   - Where: `scripts/test-network.ts:188-193`.
   - Problem: the directory is removed only in the relay's `finally` block. A SIGKILL leaves `uos-live-*/{relay.sock,hosts}` in `TMPDIR`; that can come from a timeout escalation, a CI cancellation or the out-of-memory killer.
   - Fix: have the runner delete stale `uos-live-*` directories, or create them under a parent directory owned by the runner that `runFile` removes.
7. **The new test hardcodes `/usr/bin/ip` and `/usr/bin/mount`.**
   - Where: `tests/live-network-policy.test.ts:139-143`.
   - Problem: on hosts without those exact paths, the main test segment fails.
   - Fix: look them up with the same search list that `systemTool` uses.
8. **The default live URL is defined twice.**
   - Where: `scripts/test-runner.ts:11`, `tests/live-default-model.e2e.ts:7`.
   - Problem: if one copy changes, the approved destination and the URL the test uses will differ. The run then fails safely, but with a confusing error.
   - Fix: share one constant, or have the runner always pass an explicit `BASE_URL`.

title: Follow-ups from #1135: test the same-SHA retry rollback when a previous release exists
body:
<!-- sentinel-followup:pr-1135 -->

PR #1135 (make a failed first VPS deployment resumable by the same SHA, issue #764) was merged at `3119b54d`. The finding below comes from adversarial review and was non-blocking: it did not stop the merge and is filed here as follow-up work. File and line references are to current `development` (`b4790532`). The minor (P3) items from this PR are in #1141.

## 1. The behaviour change that runs in production has no regression test

- Where: `ops/deploy.ts:338` (`restartAttempted: candidateSelected`). It reaches `restorePrevious` (`:294-309`) through `recoverFailedActivation` (`:348`). The tests are in `tests/vps-deploy-guards.test.ts`.
- Problem: when a run starts with the candidate already selected, it now sets `restartAttempted` to true, even if this run issues no restart. Production always has a previous release, so this is the path that matters there. If the retry's `systemctl reload caddy` fails, recovery now selects and restarts the previous release, checks its loopback and public identity, and records `rolled_back`. With a Deno-era predecessor it applies the cross-codec refusal instead and leaves the candidate selected. Before #1135, recovery only swapped the selector and recorded `rolled_back` while the candidate kept running. Reviewers traced the new behaviour as correct and safer than the old one, and the PR lists the gap under Known limitations. But no fixture reaches `restorePrevious` through this retry path:
  - "VPS post-ingress failure retains candidate and retries without restart" (`:746`) reaches a reload failure on a selected retry only in phase `ingress_applied`, where no recovery runs.
  - "VPS actual rollback and persistent/cleared same-SHA retry preserve immutable bytes" (`:709`) covers the restart branch only when it is entered from a first run.

  A run can leave the candidate selected and ready in three ways: the cross-codec refusal fired, the previous listener was not ready during an earlier restore, or the process died between saving `candidate_ready` and the reload.
- Fix: add a fault hook that stops the deploy after `candidate_ready` is saved and before the Caddy reload, using the current-profile fixture. A first run whose restore fails because the previous listener is not ready also works. On the retry, fail the reload again. Assert that the previous release is restarted once (restart count +1), that the public identity is the previous SHA, and that the phase is `rolled_back`. Then assert that the next retry accepts. Add a legacy-profile variant that asserts the cross-codec refusal leaves the candidate selected and the receipt unsettled.

title: Follow-ups from #1075: keep the admin token out of admin:models error output
body:
<!-- sentinel-followup:pr-1075 -->

PR #1075 ("classify admin:models BASE_URL loopback by parsed hostname", #751) was merged at `ff2fac04`. The items below are non-blocking findings from adversarial review of that PR. The PR meets #751. Line numbers refer to current `development`.

## 1. The admin token can be printed in error output

`scripts/admin-models.ts:76`, `scripts/admin-models.ts:30`, `scripts/admin-models.ts:32`

The `catch` block prints the fetch error message unchanged. If the token is not a valid header value, Bun rejects the header before connecting, and its error message contains the full value:

`Request failed: Header 'Authorization' has invalid value: 'Bearer <token>'`

That happens, for example, when a pasted token has a trailing zero-width space or an embedded newline. The deployment admin token then ends up in terminal scrollback, CI logs or agent transcripts. The old curl version never printed it.

Lines 30 and 32 also print `BASE_URL` exactly as given, including any `user:pass@` part.

**Fix:**
- Before the request, reject a token that does not match `/^[\x21-\x7e]+$/`. The error message should name the variable but not print its value.
- Remove the token from any error text before printing it at line 76.
- At lines 30 and 32, print `url.origin` (or a URL with the credentials removed) instead of the raw `BASE_URL`.
- Add a test that a token containing `\n` or U+200B fails without the token appearing in the output.

## 2. An uppercase `HTTP_PROXY` now sends loopback requests to the proxy

`scripts/admin-models.ts:70`

For `http://` URLs, curl ignores an uppercase `HTTP_PROXY`, but Bun's `fetch` honours it. Suppose only `HTTP_PROXY` is set and `NO_PROXY` does not list the loopback host. Then the default `http://localhost:8000` request goes to the proxy instead of the local server, along with any exported token, in cleartext. This contradicts the comment at lines 19-23, which says the request goes exactly to the host that was checked. Reproduced: with an unreachable proxy, the script failed, while curl with the same environment reached the local server.

**Fix:** when the hostname is loopback, bypass any proxy, for example by adding the hostname to `NO_PROXY` for the request (Bun honours it). Alternatively, document that `HTTP(S)_PROXY` and `NO_PROXY` now apply. Add a test that the loopback request is not proxied.

## 3. The token is still sent over plain `http://` to non-loopback hosts

`scripts/admin-models.ts:24-40`, `scripts/admin-models.ts:71`

With a token exported, `BASE_URL=http://ai.ubq.fi`, or a LAN address over http, sends the admin credential unencrypted. This behaviour predates #1075.

**Fix:** in `resolveEndpoint`, when a token is set and the host is not loopback, refuse `http:` or require an explicit opt-in.

## 4. The script test fails in paths with spaces or non-ASCII characters

`tests/admin-models-script.test.ts:121`

`new URL("..", import.meta.url).pathname` keeps percent-encoding. In a clone under `/Users/me/My Repos/`, the child process's working directory therefore points to a directory that does not exist, and the test fails.

**Fix:** use `fileURLToPath(new URL("..", import.meta.url))` from `node:url`, as `scripts/test-runner.ts` already does.

## 5. The README misdescribes the old behaviour

`README.md:717`

"Both tasks exit non-zero on an HTTP error rather than printing an empty result" is only half right about the old behaviour. Before #1075, `:spark` printed an empty list and plain `admin:models` printed the error body; both exited with 0.

**Fix:** reword it, for example: "Both tasks now exit non-zero on an HTTP error (previously `:spark` printed an empty list and `admin:models` printed the error body, both with exit 0)."

title: Follow-ups from #1088: order and time out provider-strip refreshes so old health is never shown as current
body:
<!-- sentinel-followup:pr-1088 -->

PR #1088 was the automated repair for #596 ("Failed provider-strip refresh leaves old health badges presented as current"). It was merged at `b89a9978` under the three-review-round rule. The items below are non-blocking findings from adversarial review of that PR. One reviewer found #596 met for its main case; the other found it not fully met. #596 was closed when the PR merged, so this issue carries the remaining work. Line numbers refer to current `development`.

## 1. #596 acceptance that is still unmet

#596's acceptance criterion: "A failed or non-2xx provider refresh marks the strip stale/unavailable or clears its previous health claims, so old badges are not presented as current."

What #1088 delivered: a single refresh can fail in several ways: a non-2xx response from `/admin/providers/selection` or `/admin/providers`, a body that does not parse, or a rejected fetch. In each case the rows are now replaced with "Provider health unavailable; previous observations cleared." (`static/admin-supervisor.js:190-209`).

What is still unmet:
- **Out-of-order refreshes.** Suppose an older refresh succeeds after a newer one has failed. The older refresh re-renders its rows with no stale marker and overwrites the "unavailable" state, so older badges are shown as current until the next 15-second tick. The reverse also happens: an older failure that finishes late wipes newer, valid rows (section 2).
- **Refreshes that never finish.** A provider request that hangs never fails, so the previous rows stay on screen as current for as long as it hangs (section 3).
- **A 2xx response with no providers.** If the selection response has an empty or missing `data.providers`, `renderProviders` returns early and the previous rows stay on screen as current (section 5). Today's server always returns the full roster, so only a schema change or a misbehaving proxy can trigger this.
- **No tests.** Nothing tests any of this, so reverting #1088 would still pass CI (section 4).

## 2. Provider refreshes are not sequenced

`static/admin-supervisor.js:194-210`, `static/admin-supervisor.js:740`

`load()` starts `void loadProviders()` on every tick and on every visibility change. There is no generation check and no abort, so whichever response finishes last wins. A reviewer reproduced both orders with a fake-DOM harness.

**Fix:** use the pattern already in `static/admin.js:3694-3705`. At the start of `loadProviders`, take `const id = ++providersLoadId`. After each `await`, return early when `id !== providersLoadId || !active`. Alternatively, keep a providers `AbortController` and abort the previous request, as `load()` already does for the sessions request.

## 3. Provider requests have no timeout

`static/admin-supervisor.js:199-202`

The two fetches have no abort signal. A stalled request leaves the old rows up with no stale marker; causes include a network drop, a VPN change or a laptop going to sleep. Every 15-second tick also adds two more pending requests to the same origin. On HTTP/1.1 these can use up the browser's connections to that host and delay other admin calls.

**Fix:**
- Pass `signal: AbortSignal.any([perRefreshController.signal, AbortSignal.timeout(REFRESH_MS - 1000)])` to both fetches.
- Mark the strip unavailable when a request times out, but not when it was aborted because a newer refresh started.
- Optionally show a "sampled at" time from `generated_at_ms`.

## 4. No regression test for the failure path

`tests/admin-supervisor-follow.test.ts:151`

The existing harness rejects every `/admin/providers*` request, and its `FakeSection.append()` discards the providers card, so no test ever reads the strip. Changing line 205 back to `if (selection) renderProviders(...)` still passes every test.

**Fix:**
- Make the harness keep the appended card.
- Add tests that render a healthy strip and then refresh with each of these failures:
  - a 502 from the selection endpoint;
  - a 500 from the health endpoint;
  - a body that does not parse;
  - a rejected fetch.
- After each failure, assert that the old "Health ..." text is gone.
- Add an out-of-order test with the fix in section 2, and a timeout test with the fix in section 3.
